verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा स राजर्षिः सदारः प्रस्थितो वनम् । भृगुतुङ्गे तपस्तप्त्वा तत्रैव च महायशाः
verses.transliteration: evamuktvā sa rājarṣiḥ sadāraḥ prasthito vanam / bhṛgutuṅge tapastaptvā tatraiva ca mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.wordMeaning: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: पालयित्वा व्रतं चार्षं तत्रैव स्वर्ग माप्तवान् । तस्य वंशास्तु पञ्चैते पुण्या देवर्षिसत्कृताः
verses.transliteration: pālayitvā vrataṃ cārṣaṃ tatraiva svarga māptavān / tasya vaṃśāstu pañcaite puṇyā devarṣisatkṛtāḥ
verses.translation: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.wordMeaning: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: यैर्व्याप्ता पृथिवी कृत्स्ना सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः । धन्यः प्रजावा नायुष्मान्कीर्त्तिमांश्च भवेन्नरः
verses.transliteration: yairvyāptā pṛthivī kṛtsnā sūryasyeva gabhastibhiḥ / dhanyaḥ prajāvā nāyuṣmānkīrttimāṃśca bhavennaraḥ
verses.translation: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.wordMeaning: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: ययातेश्चारितं सर्वं पठञ्छृण्वन्द्विजोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration: yayāteścāritaṃ sarvaṃ paṭhañchṛṇvandvijottamāḥ
verses.translation: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.wordMeaning: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे अष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ ६८॥ सूत उवाच यदोर्वंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्येष्ठस्योत्तमतेजसः । विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च गदतो मे निबोधत
verses.transliteration: iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde aṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 68// sūta uvāca yadorvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi jyeṣṭhasyottamatejasaḥ / vistareṇānupūrvyā ca gadato me nibodhata
verses.translation: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.
verses.wordMeaning: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.
verses.commentary: Sense: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.

verses.sanskrit: यदोः पुत्रा बभूवुर्हि पञ्च देवसुतोपमाः । सहस्रजिदथ श्रेष्ठः क्रोष्टुर्नीलोञ्जिको लघुः
verses.transliteration: yadoḥ putrā babhūvurhi pañca devasutopamāḥ / sahasrajidatha śreṣṭhaḥ kroṣṭurnīloñjiko laghuḥ
verses.translation: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).
verses.wordMeaning: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).
verses.commentary: Sense: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रजित्सुतः श्रीमाञ्छतजिन्नाम पार्थिवः । शतजित्तनयाः ख्यातस्त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः
verses.transliteration: sahasrajitsutaḥ śrīmāñchatajinnāma pārthivaḥ / śatajittanayāḥ khyātastrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: हैहयश्च हयस्छैव राजा वेणु हयस्तथा । हैहयस्य तु दायादो धर्मनेत्र इति श्रुतः
verses.transliteration: haihayaśca hayaschaiva rājā veṇu hayastathā / haihayasya tu dāyādo dharmanetra iti śrutaḥ
verses.translation: They were Haihaya, and the king Venuhaya. Haihaya's heir was well-known as Dharmanetra.
verses.wordMeaning: They were Haihaya, and the king Venuhaya. Haihaya's heir was well-known as Dharmanetra.
verses.commentary: Sense: They were Haihaya, and the king Venuhaya. Haihaya's heir was well-known as Dharmanetra.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मनेत्रस्य कुन्तिस्तु संक्षेयस्तस्य चात्मजः । संज्ञेयस्य तु दायादो महिष्मान्नाम पार्थिवः
verses.transliteration: dharmanetrasya kuntistu saṃkṣeyastasya cātmajaḥ / saṃjñeyasya tu dāyādo mahiṣmānnāma pārthivaḥ
verses.translation: Karttavirya performed penance for ten thousand years. His penance was extremely difficult to be performed. By means of this penance, he propitiated Datta, born of Atri.
verses.wordMeaning: Karttavirya performed penance for ten thousand years. His penance was extremely difficult to be performed. By means of this penance, he propitiated Datta, born of Atri.
verses.commentary: Sense: Karttavirya performed penance for ten thousand years. His penance was extremely difficult to be performed. By means of this penance, he propitiated Datta, born of Atri.

verses.sanskrit: आसीन्महिष्मतः पुत्रो भद्रमेनः प्रतापवान् । वाराणस्यधिपो राजा कथितः पूर्व एव हि
verses.transliteration: āsīnmahiṣmataḥ putro bhadramenaḥ pratāpavān / vārāṇasyadhipo rājā kathitaḥ pūrva eva hi
verses.translation: Datta granted him four excellently glorious boons. He chose at the out-set the first boon viz. a thousand arms.
verses.wordMeaning: Datta granted him four excellently glorious boons. He chose at the out-set the first boon viz. a thousand arms.
verses.commentary: Sense: Datta granted him four excellently glorious boons. He chose at the out-set the first boon viz. a thousand arms.

verses.sanskrit: भद्र सेनस्य दायादो दुर्मदो नाम पार्थिवः । दुर्मदस्यसुतो धीमान्कनको नाम विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration: bhadra senasya dāyādo durmado nāma pārthivaḥ / durmadasyasuto dhīmānkanako nāma viśrutaḥ
verses.translation: This entire Earth consisting of seven continents and many towns, and encircled by seven oceans was conquered by him in a manner befitting the K$atriyas.
verses.wordMeaning: This entire Earth consisting of seven continents and many towns, and encircled by seven oceans was conquered by him in a manner befitting the K$atriyas.
verses.commentary: Sense: This entire Earth consisting of seven continents and many towns, and encircled by seven oceans was conquered by him in a manner befitting the K$atriyas.

verses.sanskrit: कनकस्य तु दायादाश्चत्वारो लोकविश्रुताः । कृतवीर्यः कृताग्निश्च कृतवर्मा तथैव च
verses.transliteration: kanakasya tu dāyādāścatvāro lokaviśrutāḥ / kṛtavīryaḥ kṛtāgniśca kṛtavarmā tathaiva ca
verses.translation: He possessed a thousand arms by means of his Yogic power and that too while fighting. Just as the Yoga manifests in the case of the lord of Yogas, so also the thousand arms appear by means of Maya.
verses.wordMeaning: He possessed a thousand arms by means of his Yogic power and that too while fighting. Just as the Yoga manifests in the case of the lord of Yogas, so also the thousand arms appear by means of Maya.
verses.commentary: Sense: He possessed a thousand arms by means of his Yogic power and that too while fighting. Just as the Yoga manifests in the case of the lord of Yogas, so also the thousand arms appear by means of Maya.

verses.sanskrit: कृतौजाश्च चतुर्थो ऽभूत्कृतवीर्यात्मजोर्ऽजुनः । जज्ञे बाहुसहस्रेण सप्तद्वीपेश्वरो नृपः
verses.transliteration: kṛtaujāśca caturtho 'bhūtkṛtavīryātmajor'junaḥ / jajñe bāhusahasreṇa saptadvīpeśvaro nṛpaḥ
verses.translation: After observing the greatness and conduct of life of that saintly king, Narada, aGandharva, sang the follow- ing verse about that king:
verses.wordMeaning: After observing the greatness and conduct of life of that saintly king, Narada, aGandharva, sang the follow- ing verse about that king:
verses.commentary: Sense: After observing the greatness and conduct of life of that saintly king, Narada, aGandharva, sang the follow- ing verse about that king:

verses.sanskrit: स हि वर्षायुतं तप्त्वा तपः परमदुश्चरम् । दत्तमाराधयामास कार्त्तवीर्यो ऽत्रिसंभवम्
verses.transliteration: sa hi varṣāyutaṃ taptvā tapaḥ paramaduścaram / dattamārādhayāmāsa kārttavīryo 'trisaṃbhavam
verses.translation: On account of his thousand arms rendered tough and rough by the frequent contact with the bow-string, he shone like the autumnal Sun with his thousand rays.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of his thousand arms rendered tough and rough by the frequent contact with the bow-string, he shone like the autumnal Sun with his thousand rays.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of his thousand arms rendered tough and rough by the frequent contact with the bow-string, he shone like the autumnal Sun with his thousand rays.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै दत्तो वरान्प्रादाच्च तुरो भूरितेजसः । पूर्वं बाहुसहस्रं तु स वव्रे प्रथमं वरम्
verses.transliteration: tasmai datto varānprādācca turo bhūritejasaḥ / pūrvaṃ bāhusahasraṃ tu sa vavre prathamaṃ varam
verses.translation: With a thousand elephants, that king attacked and conquered the Royal assembly of Karkofaka in Mahi?madt and built his city there.
verses.wordMeaning: With a thousand elephants, that king attacked and conquered the Royal assembly of Karkofaka in Mahi?madt and built his city there.
verses.commentary: Sense: With a thousand elephants, that king attacked and conquered the Royal assembly of Karkofaka in Mahi?madt and built his city there.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मं ध्यायमानस्य सहसास्मान्निवारणम् । धर्मेण पृथिवीं जित्वा धर्मेणैवानुपालनम्
verses.transliteration: adharmaṃ dhyāyamānasya sahasāsmānnivāraṇam / dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ jitvā dharmeṇaivānupālanam
verses.translation: (Defective verse) That lotus-eyed king used to check the speedy waves of the ocean during the rainy season.
verses.wordMeaning: (Defective verse) That lotus-eyed king used to check the speedy waves of the ocean during the rainy season.
verses.commentary: Sense: (Defective verse) That lotus-eyed king used to check the speedy waves of the ocean during the rainy season.

verses.sanskrit: संग्रामांस्तु बहुञ्जित्वा हत्वा चारीन्सहस्रशः । संग्रामे युध्यमानस्य वधः स्यात्प्रधने मम
verses.transliteration: saṃgrāmāṃstu bahuñjitvā hatvā cārīnsahasraśaḥ / saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya vadhaḥ syātpradhane mama
verses.translation: Shaken and tossed about by him while playing, the Narmada, having garlands with golden fillets approached him in an apprehensive manner and produced a loud cry of distress released through the waves.
verses.wordMeaning: Shaken and tossed about by him while playing, the Narmada, having garlands with golden fillets approached him in an apprehensive manner and produced a loud cry of distress released through the waves.
verses.commentary: Sense: Shaken and tossed about by him while playing, the Narmada, having garlands with golden fillets approached him in an apprehensive manner and produced a loud cry of distress released through the waves.

verses.sanskrit: तेनेयं पृथिवी कृत्स्ना सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना । सप्तोदधिपरिक्षिप्ता क्षत्रेण विधिना जिता
verses.transliteration: teneyaṃ pṛthivī kṛtsnā saptadvīpā sapattanā / saptodadhiparikṣiptā kṣatreṇa vidhinā jitā
verses.translation: Once he waded through the great sea and tossed up the waves and tides by means of his thousand arms, creating an untimely high tide as though blown up by the wind.
verses.wordMeaning: Once he waded through the great sea and tossed up the waves and tides by means of his thousand arms, creating an untimely high tide as though blown up by the wind.
verses.commentary: Sense: Once he waded through the great sea and tossed up the waves and tides by means of his thousand arms, creating an untimely high tide as though blown up by the wind.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य बाहुसहस्रं तु युध्यतः किलयोगतः । योगो योगेश्वरस्येव प्रादुर्भवति मायया
verses.transliteration: tasya bāhusahasraṃ tu yudhyataḥ kilayogataḥ / yogo yogeśvarasyeva prādurbhavati māyayā
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: तेन सप्तसु द्वीपेषु सप्तयज्ञशतानि वै । कृतानि विधिना राज्ञा श्रूयते मुनिसत्तमाः
verses.transliteration: tena saptasu dvīpeṣu saptayajñaśatāni vai / kṛtāni vidhinā rājñā śrūyate munisattamāḥ
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे यज्ञा महाबाहोस्तस्यामन्भूरितेजसः । सर्वे काञ्चनवेदीकाः सर्वे यूपैश्च काञ्चनैः
verses.transliteration: sarve yajñā mahābāhostasyāmanbhūritejasaḥ / sarve kāñcanavedīkāḥ sarve yūpaiśca kāñcanaiḥ
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वैर्देवैर्महाभागै र्विमानस्थैरलङ्कृताः । गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च नित्यमेवोपशोभिताः
verses.transliteration: sarvairdevairmahābhāgai rvimānasthairalaṅkṛtāḥ / gandharvairapsarobhiśca nityamevopaśobhitāḥ
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य राज्ञो जगौ गाथां गन्धर्वो नारदस्तदा । चरितं तस्य राजर्षेर्महिमानं निरीक्ष्य च
verses.transliteration: tasya rājño jagau gāthāṃ gandharvo nāradastadā / caritaṃ tasya rājarṣermahimānaṃ nirīkṣya ca
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: न नूनं कार्त्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति मानवाः । यज्ञैर्दानैस्तपोभिश्च विक्रमेण श्रुतेन च
verses.transliteration: na nūnaṃ kārttavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti mānavāḥ / yajñairdānaistapobhiśca vikrameṇa śrutena ca
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: द्वीपेषु सप्तसु स वै धन्वी खड्गी शारासनी । रथी राजा सानुचरो योगाच्चैवानुदृश्यते
verses.transliteration: dvīpeṣu saptasu sa vai dhanvī khaḍgī śārāsanī / rathī rājā sānucaro yogāccaivānudṛśyate
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: अनष्टद्रव्यता चासीन्न क्लेशो न च विभ्रमः । प्रभावेण महाराज्ञः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षितः
verses.transliteration: anaṣṭadravyatā cāsīnna kleśo na ca vibhramaḥ / prabhāveṇa mahārājñaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣitaḥ
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चाशीतिसहस्राणि वर्षाणां स नराधिपः । स सर्वरत्नभाक्स म्राट् चक्रवर्ती बभूव ह
verses.transliteration: pañcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa narādhipaḥ / sa sarvaratnabhāksa mrāṭ cakravartī babhūva ha
verses.translation: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.wordMeaning: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: On account of the curse of that intelligent sage, Rama became the cause of his death. In fact this boon had been chosen by that king himself formerly.

verses.sanskrit: स एष पशुपालो ऽभूत्क्षेत्रपालस्तथै व च । स एव वृष्ट्या पर्जन्यो योगित्वादर्जुनो ऽभवत्

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महोपुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते कार्त्तवीर्यसंभवो नाम एकोनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ऋषय ऊचुः किमर्थं तु वनं दग्धमापवस्य महात्मनः । कार्त्तवीर्येण विक्रम्य तन्नः प्रब्रूहि पृच्छताम्
verses.transliteration: iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahopurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite kārttavīryasaṃbhavo nāma ekonasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ṛṣaya ūcuḥ kimarthaṃ tu vanaṃ dagdhamāpavasya mahātmanaḥ / kārttavīryeṇa vikramya tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām
verses.translation: Aditya (the Sun-god) approached Karttavirya in the guise of a Brahmana and said, "Give me food till I am satis- fied. Because I am undoubtedly the Sun-god." O lord, tell me, with what will you be satisfied, O Sun- god? What type of food should I serve you? I shall do so after hearing from you. "Give unto me as food all immovable beings, O most excellent one among donors. I shall be satisfied with it, O king, and not with anything else." "All the immovable beings cannot be burnt by the fiery splendour of a human being, O most excellent one among those who blaze, I make my obeisance unto you." Out of anger, he cursed the saintly king in the manner already recounted to you by me. Svahi, the most excellent one among Svahavans (i.e. those who perform Tajnas where the Mantra 'Svaha' is repeat- ed) was the son ofVrjinlvan. Svahi's son Ruseku* became a king and the most excellent one among donors. * Persons conversant with Puragas praise Aksara* as the son of Prthusravas. Suyajfia was the son of Aksara and Usanas was his son. Our text dropped Sineyu as the son of Usanas and named his grandson Marutta as the son of Usanas vide AIHT, Five sons of great strength and prowess were born to Rukmakavaca. They could pierce the enemies and kill inimical warriors. They were Rukmesu, Prthurukma, Jyamagha, Parigha and Hari. The father established Parigha and Hari in the land of Videha. Rukmesu became king (as successor to his father,1) and Prthurukma became his dependant. Thus cheated (and defeated) by them, Jyamagha2 lived in a hermitage though (he was entitled to be) a king. On being told thus, she replied "To which son docs she belong to be called my daughter-in-law? By means of her severe and terrible penance, the exalted noble lady Saibya, in her old age, gave birth to her son Vidarbha. AlHT. names Par&vft instead of Rukmesu as the successor to Rukmakavaca. In regard to that race of kings, Brahmanas conver- sant with the Puranas sing the following verses. They glorify the good qualities of the noble-souled Devavrdha. Once, at the close of night, that excellent person among riders in the chariot (a great warrior) viz. Satrajit went in his chariot to the banks (of the river) in order to take water for offering libations to the sun. On hearing this, the Sun-god removed the excellent jewel Syamantaka1 from his own neck and tied it round the neck of the king. Thereupon, the king saw him in his physical form. On seeing him, he was delighted and he carried on a pleasant talk with him for a short while. The king wore that jewel when he entered the city. He made the entire city wonder-struck and entered his harem. With great love, that king Satrajit gave that divine excellent jewel Syamantaka to his brother Prasena. Parjanya (god of clouds and rain) would shower plenty of rain in that country where this jewel named Syaman- taka happened to exist. There would be no danger from ailments or epidemics in that country. Govinda (Krsia) expressed his desire to have that excellent jewel Syamantaka from Prasena, but did not get it. Although he was powerful enough, he did not take it by force. Once Prasena bedecked himself with that jewel and went for hunting. For the sake of Syamantaka (i.e. on account of it) he met with a terrible death from a lion. Jambavan, the king of bears, killed that lion. He took the divine jewel and entered his cave. Compare the story of Syamantaka in Bh.P.X.Chs 56 and 57. Elderly persons among the Vrsnis and Andhakas considered that murder of Prasena an act of Krsna who was covetous of the jewel. They suspected him alone. The lord, the destroyer of enemies, who jvas more powerful than they did not brook that false accusation. So he roamed about in the forest to trace Prasena. After reporting to her husband (i.e. Krsna) the Hari (Krsna) performed the obsequies of Pantfavas who were supposed to have been burnt in the lac palace at Varanavata. He engaged Satyaki in activities of welfare* (?). for the brothers. Then a fierce battle ensued between Bhoja and Krsna. Satadhanva looked for Akrura in every direction. Akrura left Bhoja and Srikrsna without bringing about any truce between them. Though he was able to fight, he did not own loyalty, due to perfidy. Then Satadhanvan became frightened. He decided to go away from that place. Hrdaya (the mare of Satadhanvan) ran more than a hundred Yojanas. The mare named Hrdaya belonged to Bhoja. It was reputed as one capable of going a hundred Yojanas. It was a divine mare with which he fought with Krsna. On seeing Hrdaya exhausted due to the fast running at the close of the hundredth Yojana of the journey and on observing the misfortune (?) of the chariot, Satadhanvan began to run on foot. Then, due to fatigue and affliction, O Brahmanas, that vital breath of that mare went up in the sky. Then Krsna said to Rama. "O mighty one, wait here. I have found out that there is a defect in the mare. I shall go on foot and take away the excellent jewel Syamantaka". He did not see Syamantaka (with him). When Krsna returned after killing Bhoja of great strength, the wielder of plough (i.e. Bala-Rama) said to him "Give me the jewel*'. "I tolerate this since you are my brother. Welfare unto you. I am going away. I have nothing to do with Dvaraka, you and the Vrsnis." Thereafter, Rama, the suppressor of foes entered Mithila. With the offering of all desirable objects he was honoured by the king of Mithila himself. This intelligent noble-minded son of Gandini (Akrura) adopted initiation along with Kavaca (coat of mail) as protection, for keeping Syamantaka. Those sacrifices of that noble-souled one are famous as AkrUrayajhas. In all of them, food and monetary gifts were in plenty. All of them yielded everything one desired. Then king Duryodhana went to Mithila. The lord had a training in mace-fighting under Balabhadra. The training was usually of a divine nature. Akrura, a powerful leader of men, came back along with the Andhakas after killing Satrughna along with Bandhuman. When Danapati (i.e. Akrura) returned to Dvaraka once again, the thousand-eyed lord (Indra) rained every- where (even) within the ocean. In order to gain the love (of Krsna), O leading sages, Akrura, the glorious one gave his sister ( in marriage ) to Vasudeva, a girl honoured by everyone for her good conduct. By means of his Yogic power, Krsna understood that the jewel Syamantaka was with Babhru (i.e. Akrura). Hence, he spoke thus to Akrura in the open Assembly hall. Then, at the instance of Krsna, the highly intelli- gent Babhru handed over, without hesitation and mental strain, the jewel (to Krsna) in the Assembly of all Satvatas. Then Krsna, the suppressor of enemies, became delighted in his mind. He returned to Babhru the jewel he had obtained from Babhru, by a straightforward deal. After obtaining from Kf§na the excellent jewel Syamantaka, the son of Gandini wore it and shone like the Sun. He who understands this false accusation of the lord and the excellent way in which the lord cleared himself, will not at all be a victim of false accusation.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षिता सतु राजर्षिः प्रजानामिति नः श्रुतम् । कथं सरक्षिता भूत्वा नाशयेत तपोवनम्
verses.transliteration: rakṣitā satu rājarṣiḥ prajānāmiti naḥ śrutam / kathaṃ sarakṣitā bhūtvā nāśayeta tapovanam
verses.translation: That king of Ka£i greatly honoured Svaphalka and made him stay there. The chastiser of Paka (i.e. Indra) showered rain on account of the stay of Svaphalka. Svaphalka obtained as his wife the daughter of the king of Kasi, named Gandini. Every day she gave a cow as a gift to a Brahmana.1 A popular etymology of GSxhdini. The daughter of the king of KasI bore four sons to Satyaka viz. — Kukura, Bhajamana, Suci and Kambalabarhis. They were Devaka and Ugrasena. Both of them were on a par with those born of divine womb. Heroic sons comparable to the Devas were born to Devaka. They were Devavan, Upadeva, Sudeva, and Deva- raksita. They had seven sisters. He gave them to Vasudeva in marriage. A scholarly son named Kambalabarhis was born to Devabahu. Asamaujas was his son. (Another son) Susamaujas was very famous. Krsna gave Sucandra and Vasurupa (as sons in adoption) to Asamaujas of whom no son was born. He who repeats the names of and glorifies this race of Andhakas every day, attains an extensive family of himself. There is no doubt in this matter. Sura begot Devamldhvan (Dcvaml<jhusa) of Asmaki. Ten persons were bom of Mari si from Sura. Maris! belonged to the Bhoja family. Bimba, Upabimba, Sattvadanta and Mahaujas — these four persons of great strength are well known as the sons ofBhadra (?) In these circumstances, Visnu, the lord of worlds, became Prajapati once again (being bom) as the long- lived Krsna. Subhadra, who used to speak pleasantly well (Bhadrabhasini) was bom subsequent to Krsna. This lady who delighted the family of Vr$ni became well renowned later as Krsna and Subhadra. Santideva gave birth to Janastambha the illustrious scion of the family of Sauri. To the other lady, a powerful heroic son of Vasudeva was born. He was the Nisada (forester) n£med Jara (?). He was the foremost archer. Anadhrsti begot of Asmaki, a powerful son Srad- dhadeva. He was a destroyer of enemies. All his enemies had receded from him. With pleasure Krsna gave his sons Carudesna and Samba for adoption to Garujusa who had no children. These two sons were well up in the use of arms. They were endowed with highly laudable characteristics. He who duly observes holy rites and reads this story of the birth of Krsna or narrates it to a Brahmana, shall obtain great happiness. Krsna, the lord of the Devas, the Prajapati (lord or procreator of subjects) who was originally Lord Narayana, was born among human beings for the sake of sport. ( Partially defective text). The lord had created Prajapati (god Brahma) the primordial Being from a lotus. The lord well-known as Visnu became the younger brother of Indra after being born as the son of Aditi. Devas propitiated the omnipresent Lord for being born as the son of Aditi. Causing delusion to the subjects through his Maya (illusive Powerj, the lord incarnated and the lord of the Devas (i.e. Indra) caused shower of flowers from the sky. With words full of auspicious purport and signi- ficance, thousands of great sages, along with the Gandharvas eulogised and prayed to Madhusudana. Being permitted by the lord, the father took him to the abode of Nanda the cowherd (who was staying) in the house of Ugrasena and handed him to Yasoda. Yasoda and Devaki had become pregnant at the same time. Yasoda was the wife of Nandagopa, the head of cowherds. * Guarding the son bom to him, Vasudeva of great fame, handed over his son to Yasoda and took the girl with him. The evil-minded (Kamsa) handed the girl back (to Vasudeva) and said with pleasure — "She is my daughter in the same way as yours. There is no doubt in this. O heroic one, I will not kill her. Let her go wherever she pleases". Wherefor did the Bhoja king Kariisa kill the infant sons of Vasudcva? It behoves you to clarify this. At the marriage of Dcvaki and Vasudeva the intelligent Kamsa acted as the charioteer. At that time he was the crown-Prince. Then in the sky rose the speech of some incompre- hensible person. It was a divine speech. It was very loud and witnessed by the people of the world merely because the name of Kamsa was uttered by it. "O Kamsa, out of afTection, you are taking your sister by means of a chariot. The eighth child of that lady shall be your killer". On hearing that aerial voice, Kamsa, the foolish one, became distressed. He drew his sword and became intent on killing her. The Valorous Vasudeva of great power said to Kamsa the son of Ugrasena, out of friendship or love. — "O scion of the family of Yadavas, you are a K$atriya and it does not behove you to kill a woman. In this matter (under reference) a certain remedy has been found out by me. O lord of the Earth, I shall hand over to you the eighth son that will be born of her. With him, you can do what you deem proper. O munificent one, do not behave now in.the way you wish. In this manner, O excellent one among men, this aerial voice too will not be erroneous". On regaining his wife, Vasudeva became delighted. The foolish-minded Karhsa of evil deeds killed his sons. WhenDharma (Virtue) became lost, Visnu himself was bom in the family of Vrsni in order to re-establish Dharma and annihilate Asuras. Sahgramajit, Satajit and Sahasrajit — these were glorified as the sons of Visvaksena born of Sudevl. The children of the daughter of Nagnajit were these — viz. Vrka, VrkaSva, Vrkajit, Mitrabahu and Sunltha were sons. Vrjini, the excellent lady, was her daughter. These and others constitute thousands of sons. Understand that it is mentioned that Vasudeva's sons were about a million. Eighty thousand among them were- great heroes and experts in war. Thereof her sons viz. Ananda, Kanaka and Sveta were well-known. They shone splendidly in battles. She had a daughter also named Sveta. Gitra, Sura and Gitraratha were the sons of Agavaha. Gitrasena was his son. He had a daughter Citravati Tumba had two sons viz. Tumba (?) and Tumbavarcas. Bhurindrasena and Bhuri were the sons of Gavesana. Kasya ( Princess of Kasi) bore five courageous and strong sons to Samba. They are glorified as five shining heroes beginning with Satya. Those powerful Asuras who were killed in the battles between the Devas and Asuras are born here among human beings. They harass human beings. Thus the progeny of Vfsnis has been glorified succinctly and in detail. That must be glorified by one who is desirous of achievement of fame.

verses.wordMeaning: Then the grandfather (i.e. Brahm&) himself came there and prevented Usanas and Rudra, from fighting. He restored T&ra to Angiras ( Brhaspati).
