verses.sanskrit: संयोज्या त्मानमेवं स पर्णाशजलमस्पृशत्
verses.transliteration: saṃyojyā tmānamevaṃ sa parṇāśajalamaspṛśat
verses.translation: On seeing Tara, the lady of moon-like face, pregnant, the Brahmana Brhaspati said — "You cast off the foetus immediately.
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing Tara, the lady of moon-like face, pregnant, the Brahmana Brhaspati said — "You cast off the foetus immediately.
verses.commentary: Sense: On seeing Tara, the lady of moon-like face, pregnant, the Brahmana Brhaspati said — "You cast off the foetus immediately.

verses.sanskrit: सा चोपस्पर्शनात्तस्य चकार प्रियमापगा । कल्याणत्वान्नरपतेस्तस्य सा निम्नगोत्तमा
verses.transliteration: sā copasparśanāttasya cakāra priyamāpagā / kalyāṇatvānnarapatestasya sā nimnagottamā
verses.translation: Your womb belongs to me and therefore no other child should ever be born there". So Tara discharged the child in the womb that was blazing like fire.
verses.wordMeaning: Your womb belongs to me and therefore no other child should ever be born there". So Tara discharged the child in the womb that was blazing like fire.
verses.commentary: Sense: Your womb belongs to me and therefore no other child should ever be born there". So Tara discharged the child in the womb that was blazing like fire.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्तयाभिपरीताङ्गी जगामाथ विनिश्चयम् । नाभिगच्छामि तां नारीं यस्यामेवंविधः सुतः
verses.transliteration: cintayābhiparītāṅgī jagāmātha viniścayam / nābhigacchāmi tāṃ nārīṃ yasyāmevaṃvidhaḥ sutaḥ
verses.translation: The moment he was born that lord assumed the body of the Devas. Therefore the Suras became suspicious and told Tara.
verses.wordMeaning: The moment he was born that lord assumed the body of the Devas. Therefore the Suras became suspicious and told Tara.
verses.commentary: Sense: The moment he was born that lord assumed the body of the Devas. Therefore the Suras became suspicious and told Tara.

verses.sanskrit: भवेत्सर्वगुणोपेतो राज्ञो देवावृधस्य हि । तस्मादस्य स्वयं चाहं भवाम्यद्य सहव्रता
verses.transliteration: bhavetsarvaguṇopeto rājño devāvṛdhasya hi / tasmādasya svayaṃ cāhaṃ bhavāmyadya sahavratā
verses.translation: The daughter of the king (i.e. Ili) gave birth to his son. Therefore Pururavas, the son of Ila, became his son of great splendour.
verses.wordMeaning: The daughter of the king (i.e. Ili) gave birth to his son. Therefore Pururavas, the son of Ila, became his son of great splendour.
verses.commentary: Sense: The daughter of the king (i.e. Ili) gave birth to his son. Therefore Pururavas, the son of Ila, became his son of great splendour.

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञे तस्याः स्वयं हृत्स्थो भावस्तस्य यथेरितः । अथ भूत्वा कुमारी तु सा चिन्तापरमेव च
verses.transliteration: jajñe tasyāḥ svayaṃ hṛtstho bhāvastasya yatheritaḥ / atha bhūtvā kumārī tu sā cintāparameva ca
verses.translation: Setting aside her personal prestige, Urva£I, the reput- ed (celestial damsel), chose as her husband that expounder of Brahman who had complete control of his sense organs, was conversant with dharma, and truthful in speech.
verses.wordMeaning: Setting aside her personal prestige, Urva£I, the reput- ed (celestial damsel), chose as her husband that expounder of Brahman who had complete control of his sense organs, was conversant with dharma, and truthful in speech.
verses.commentary: Sense: Setting aside her personal prestige, Urva£I, the reput- ed (celestial damsel), chose as her husband that expounder of Brahman who had complete control of his sense organs, was conversant with dharma, and truthful in speech.

verses.sanskrit: वरयामास राजानं तामियेष स पार्थिवः । तस्यामाधत्त गर्भे स तेजस्विनमुदा रधीः
verses.transliteration: varayāmāsa rājānaṃ tāmiyeṣa sa pārthivaḥ / tasyāmādhatta garbhe sa tejasvinamudā radhīḥ
verses.translation: The king of great vigour accompanied by Urvagi sported with excessive joy in these important parks and forests frequented by the Suras.
verses.wordMeaning: The king of great vigour accompanied by Urvagi sported with excessive joy in these important parks and forests frequented by the Suras.
verses.commentary: Sense: The king of great vigour accompanied by Urvagi sported with excessive joy in these important parks and forests frequented by the Suras.

verses.sanskrit: अथ सा नवमे मासि सुषुवे सरिता वरा । पुत्रं सर्वगुणोपेतं बभ्रुं देवावृधत्तदा
verses.transliteration: atha sā navame māsi suṣuve saritā varā / putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ babhruṃ devāvṛdhattadā
verses.translation: Tell us the misdemeanour of the king for whicli the Gandharva divine lady UrvasI left off the king of human birth and came back to heaven.
verses.wordMeaning: Tell us the misdemeanour of the king for whicli the Gandharva divine lady UrvasI left off the king of human birth and came back to heaven.
verses.commentary: Sense: Tell us the misdemeanour of the king for whicli the Gandharva divine lady UrvasI left off the king of human birth and came back to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र वंशे पुराणज्ञा गाथां गायन्ति वै द्विजाः । गुणान्देवावृधस्यापि कीर्तयन्तो महात्मनः
verses.transliteration: tatra vaṃśe purāṇajñā gāthāṃ gāyanti vai dvijāḥ / guṇāndevāvṛdhasyāpi kīrtayanto mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: Overwhelmed with the curse of a Brahmana (or of Brahma), she came to the world of human beings. For the sake of getting herself released from the curse, she stipulated certain conditions.
verses.wordMeaning: Overwhelmed with the curse of a Brahmana (or of Brahma), she came to the world of human beings. For the sake of getting herself released from the curse, she stipulated certain conditions.
verses.commentary: Sense: Overwhelmed with the curse of a Brahmana (or of Brahma), she came to the world of human beings. For the sake of getting herself released from the curse, she stipulated certain conditions.

verses.sanskrit: यथैव शृणुमो दूरात्सपंश्यामस्तथान्तिकात् । बभ्रुः श्रेष्ठो मनुष्याणां देवैर्देवावृथः समः
verses.transliteration: yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrātsapaṃśyāmastathāntikāt / babhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devairdevāvṛthaḥ samaḥ
verses.translation: Through the curse of Yuvana$va, Ganga gave birth from half of her part to Kaverl the praise-worthy wife of Jahnu, the most excellent of all rivers.
verses.wordMeaning: Through the curse of Yuvana$va, Ganga gave birth from half of her part to Kaverl the praise-worthy wife of Jahnu, the most excellent of all rivers.
verses.commentary: Sense: Through the curse of Yuvana$va, Ganga gave birth from half of her part to Kaverl the praise-worthy wife of Jahnu, the most excellent of all rivers.

verses.sanskrit: पुरुषाः पञ्चषष्टिश्च सहस्राणि च सप्ततिः । येमृतत्वमनुप्राप्ता बब्रोर्देवावृधादपि
verses.transliteration: puruṣāḥ pañcaṣaṣṭiśca sahasrāṇi ca saptatiḥ / yemṛtatvamanuprāptā babrordevāvṛdhādapi
verses.translation: Jahnu begot of Kaverl a beloved son of great virtue named Sunaha. His son was Ajaka.
verses.wordMeaning: Jahnu begot of Kaverl a beloved son of great virtue named Sunaha. His son was Ajaka.
verses.commentary: Sense: Jahnu begot of Kaverl a beloved son of great virtue named Sunaha. His son was Ajaka.

verses.sanskrit: यज्वा दानपतिर्धीरो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाग्बुधः । कीर्त्तिमांश्च महाभोजः सात्त्वतानां महारथः
verses.transliteration: yajvā dānapatirdhīro brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāgbudhaḥ / kīrttimāṃśca mahābhojaḥ sāttvatānāṃ mahārathaḥ
verses.translation: Ajaka's heir Balakasva of great fame, became a habitual hunter. Kusa is remembered as his son.
verses.wordMeaning: Ajaka's heir Balakasva of great fame, became a habitual hunter. Kusa is remembered as his son.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ajaka's heir Balakasva of great fame, became a habitual hunter. Kusa is remembered as his son.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यान्ववायः सुमहान्भोजा ये भुवि विश्रुताः । गान्धारी चैव माद्री च धृष्टैर्भार्ये बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration: tasyānvavāyaḥ sumahānbhojā ye bhuvi viśrutāḥ / gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca dhṛṣṭairbhārye babhūvatuḥ
verses.translation: Ku$a had four sons of divine lustre and refulgence viz. Kusamba, Kusa-nabha, Amurtarayasa and Vasu.
verses.wordMeaning: Ku$a had four sons of divine lustre and refulgence viz. Kusamba, Kusa-nabha, Amurtarayasa and Vasu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ku$a had four sons of divine lustre and refulgence viz. Kusamba, Kusa-nabha, Amurtarayasa and Vasu.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धारी जनयामास सुमित्रं मित्रनन्दनम् । साद्री युधाजितं पुत्रं ततो मीढ्वांसमेव च
verses.transliteration: gāndhārī janayāmāsa sumitraṃ mitranandanam / sādrī yudhājitaṃ putraṃ tato mīḍhvāṃsameva ca
verses.translation: Kusika (? Kusaniibha) the excellent king performed a penance seeking a son. When a hundred years were complet- ed, Indra noticed him.
verses.wordMeaning: Kusika (? Kusaniibha) the excellent king performed a penance seeking a son. When a hundred years were complet- ed, Indra noticed him.
verses.commentary: Sense: Kusika (? Kusaniibha) the excellent king performed a penance seeking a son. When a hundred years were complet- ed, Indra noticed him.

verses.sanskrit: अनमित्रं शिनं चैव ताबुभौ पुरुषोत्तमौ । अनमित्रसुतो निघ्नो निघ्नस्य द्वौ बभूवतुः
verses.transliteration: anamitraṃ śinaṃ caiva tābubhau puruṣottamau / anamitrasuto nighno nighnasya dvau babhūvatuḥ
verses.translation: Paurukutsi (daughter ofPurukutsa) became the wife of Gadhi. At first a splendid girl of exalted fortune was born of her known by the name of Satyavatl.1
verses.wordMeaning: Paurukutsi (daughter ofPurukutsa) became the wife of Gadhi. At first a splendid girl of exalted fortune was born of her known by the name of Satyavatl.1
verses.commentary: Sense: Paurukutsi (daughter ofPurukutsa) became the wife of Gadhi. At first a splendid girl of exalted fortune was born of her known by the name of Satyavatl.1

verses.sanskrit: प्रसेनश्च महाभागः सत्राजिच्च सुताबुभौ । तस्य सत्राजितः सूर्यः सखा प्राणसमो ऽभवत्
verses.transliteration: prasenaśca mahābhāgaḥ satrājicca sutābubhau / tasya satrājitaḥ sūryaḥ sakhā prāṇasamo 'bhavat
verses.translation: This Caru should be eaten by you, O splendid lady and that Caru by your mother. To her will be born a lustrous son. a bull among K$atriyas, who can never be con- quered by Ksatriyas in battle and who will be able to slay even prominent K$atriya warriors. So you also, O lady of
verses.wordMeaning: This Caru should be eaten by you, O splendid lady and that Caru by your mother. To her will be born a lustrous son. a bull among K$atriyas, who can never be con- quered by Ksatriyas in battle and who will be able to slay even prominent K$atriya warriors. So you also, O lady of
verses.commentary: Sense: This Caru should be eaten by you, O splendid lady and that Caru by your mother. To her will be born a lustrous son. a bull among K$atriyas, who can never be con- quered by Ksatriyas in battle and who will be able to slay even prominent K$atriya warriors. So you also, O lady of

verses.sanskrit: स कदाचिन्निशापाये रथेन रथिनां वरः । तोयं कूलात्समुद्धर्तुमुपस्थातुं ययौरविम्
verses.transliteration: sa kadācinniśāpāye rathena rathināṃ varaḥ / toyaṃ kūlātsamuddhartumupasthātuṃ yayauravim
verses.translation: Pargiter gives Kuiasva as the name of Kusa's son and Kuiika was. Kusasva's son (AIHT, ).
verses.wordMeaning: Pargiter gives Kuiasva as the name of Kusa's son and Kuiika was. Kusasva's son (AIHT, ).
verses.commentary: Sense: Pargiter gives Kuiasva as the name of Kusa's son and Kuiika was. Kusasva's son (AIHT, ).

verses.sanskrit: तस्योपतिष्ठतः सूर्यं विवस्वानग्रतः स्थितः । सुस्पष्टमूर्त्तिर्भगवांस्तेजोमण्डलवान्विभुः
verses.transliteration: tasyopatiṣṭhataḥ sūryaṃ vivasvānagrataḥ sthitaḥ / suspaṣṭamūrttirbhagavāṃstejomaṇḍalavānvibhuḥ
verses.translation: On being told thus, the sage said "O excellent lady, this has never been thought of by me or by you. This has never
verses.wordMeaning: On being told thus, the sage said "O excellent lady, this has never been thought of by me or by you. This has never
verses.commentary: Sense: On being told thus, the sage said "O excellent lady, this has never been thought of by me or by you. This has never

verses.sanskrit: अथ राजा विवस्वन्तमुवाच स्थितमग्रतः । यथैव व्योम्नि पश्यामि त्वामहं ज्योतिषां पते
verses.transliteration: atha rājā vivasvantamuvāca sthitamagrataḥ / yathaiva vyomni paśyāmi tvāmahaṃ jyotiṣāṃ pate
verses.translation: Therefore, Satyavati gave birth to Jamadagni, a son of the Bhrgu family, of quiescent nature, having perfect control over his sense-organs and devoted to the performance of penance.
verses.wordMeaning: Therefore, Satyavati gave birth to Jamadagni, a son of the Bhrgu family, of quiescent nature, having perfect control over his sense-organs and devoted to the performance of penance.
verses.commentary: Sense: Therefore, Satyavati gave birth to Jamadagni, a son of the Bhrgu family, of quiescent nature, having perfect control over his sense-organs and devoted to the performance of penance.

verses.sanskrit: तेजोमण्डलिनं चैव तथैवाप्यग्रतः स्थितम् । को विशेषो विवस्वंस्ते सख्येनोपगतस्य वै
verses.transliteration: tejomaṇḍalinaṃ caiva tathaivāpyagrataḥ sthitam / ko viśeṣo vivasvaṃste sakhyenopagatasya vai
verses.translation: Formerly, there had been an interchange of the Carus belonging to Rudra and Visnu. Since he ate (i.e. since he was born as a result of his mother eating) the fire (Caru) belong- ing to Visnu, lie became Jamadagni
verses.wordMeaning: Formerly, there had been an interchange of the Carus belonging to Rudra and Visnu. Since he ate (i.e. since he was born as a result of his mother eating) the fire (Caru) belong- ing to Visnu, lie became Jamadagni
verses.commentary: Sense: Formerly, there had been an interchange of the Carus belonging to Rudra and Visnu. Since he ate (i.e. since he was born as a result of his mother eating) the fire (Caru) belong- ing to Visnu, lie became Jamadagni

verses.sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा स भगवान्मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् । स्वकण्ठादवमुच्याथ बबन्ध नृपतेस्तदा
verses.transliteration: etacchrutvā sa bhagavānmaṇiratnaṃ syamantakam / svakaṇṭhādavamucyātha babandha nṛpatestadā
verses.translation: After getting Visvamitra as his heir, Gadhi the son of Kusika (or descendant of Kusika) attained the status equal to that of a Brahminical sage. He was chosen by Brahma (as such ).
verses.wordMeaning: After getting Visvamitra as his heir, Gadhi the son of Kusika (or descendant of Kusika) attained the status equal to that of a Brahminical sage. He was chosen by Brahma (as such ).
verses.commentary: Sense: After getting Visvamitra as his heir, Gadhi the son of Kusika (or descendant of Kusika) attained the status equal to that of a Brahminical sage. He was chosen by Brahma (as such ).

verses.sanskrit: ततो विग्रहवन्तं तं ददर्श नृपतिस्तदा । प्रीतिमानथ तं दृष्ट्वा मुहूर्त्तं कृतवान्कथाम्
verses.transliteration: tato vigrahavantaṃ taṃ dadarśa nṛpatistadā / prītimānatha taṃ dṛṣṭvā muhūrttaṃ kṛtavānkathām
verses.translation: Satyavati of great sanctity and devoted to truth- ful vows and observances flowed as the great river named Kausiki. Kausiki the most excellent and distinguished river began to flow.
verses.wordMeaning: Satyavati of great sanctity and devoted to truth- ful vows and observances flowed as the great river named Kausiki. Kausiki the most excellent and distinguished river began to flow.
verses.commentary: Sense: Satyavati of great sanctity and devoted to truth- ful vows and observances flowed as the great river named Kausiki. Kausiki the most excellent and distinguished river began to flow.

verses.sanskrit: तमभिप्रस्थितं भूयो विवस्वन्तं स सत्रजित् । प्रोवाचाग्निसवर्णं त्वां येन लोकः प्रपश्यति
verses.transliteration: tamabhiprasthitaṃ bhūyo vivasvantaṃ sa satrajit / provācāgnisavarṇaṃ tvāṃ yena lokaḥ prapaśyati
verses.translation: A comparison of this list with that given in Mt.P., Baudh&yana, Aival&yana, Apastamba and Katyayana shows that our author is not exhaus- tive in giving the Gotras of the Kuiika clan, (vide *Mt.P. — a Study* p -409)
verses.wordMeaning: A comparison of this list with that given in Mt.P., Baudh&yana, Aival&yana, Apastamba and Katyayana shows that our author is not exhaus- tive in giving the Gotras of the Kuiika clan, (vide *Mt.P. — a Study* p -409)
verses.commentary: Sense: A comparison of this list with that given in Mt.P., Baudh&yana, Aival&yana, Apastamba and Katyayana shows that our author is not exhaus- tive in giving the Gotras of the Kuiika clan, (vide *Mt.P. — a Study* p -409)

verses.sanskrit: तदेतन्मणिरत्नं मे भगवन्दातुमर्हसि । स्यमं तकं नाममणिं दत्तवांस्तस्य भास्करः
verses.transliteration: tadetanmaṇiratnaṃ me bhagavandātumarhasi / syamaṃ takaṃ nāmamaṇiṃ dattavāṃstasya bhāskaraḥ
verses.translation: A rich man desirous of religious merit and virtue may invite excellent Brahmanas and perform Yajftas with wealth acquired by unjust means. But he does not attain the benefit of the righteous act.
verses.wordMeaning: A rich man desirous of religious merit and virtue may invite excellent Brahmanas and perform Yajftas with wealth acquired by unjust means. But he does not attain the benefit of the righteous act.
verses.commentary: Sense: A rich man desirous of religious merit and virtue may invite excellent Brahmanas and perform Yajftas with wealth acquired by unjust means. But he does not attain the benefit of the righteous act.

verses.sanskrit: स तमामुच्य नगरीं प्रविवेश महीपतिः । विस्मापयित्वाथ ततः पुरीमन्तःपुरं ययौ
verses.transliteration: sa tamāmucya nagarīṃ praviveśa mahīpatiḥ / vismāpayitvātha tataḥ purīmantaḥpuraṃ yayau
verses.translation: If a man gives to the deserving persons wealth accumulated through just means, if a person worships and distributes gifts without cherishing desires in his mind, he acquires the fruit of those charitable gifts. That gift results in pleasure and happiness. One attains worldly pleasures through
verses.wordMeaning: If a man gives to the deserving persons wealth accumulated through just means, if a person worships and distributes gifts without cherishing desires in his mind, he acquires the fruit of those charitable gifts. That gift results in pleasure and happiness.…
verses.commentary: Sense: If a man gives to the deserving persons wealth accumulated through just means, if a person worships and distributes gifts without cherishing desires in his mind, he acquires the fruit of those charitable gifts. That gift results in pleasure and happiness.…

verses.sanskrit: स प्रसेनाय तद्दिव्यं मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् । ददौ भ्रात्रे नरपतिः प्रेम्णा सत्राजिदुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: sa prasenāya taddivyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam / dadau bhrātre narapatiḥ premṇā satrājiduttamam
verses.translation: Ayus had five noble-souled sons of great strength. Those kings were born of Prabha, the daughter ofSvarbhanu.
verses.wordMeaning: Ayus had five noble-souled sons of great strength. Those kings were born of Prabha, the daughter ofSvarbhanu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ayus had five noble-souled sons of great strength. Those kings were born of Prabha, the daughter ofSvarbhanu.

verses.sanskrit: स्यमन्तको नाम मणिर्यस्मिन्राष्ट्रे स्थितो भवेत् । कामवर्षी च पर्जन्यो न च व्याधिभयं तथा
verses.transliteration: syamantako nāma maṇiryasminrāṣṭre sthito bhavet / kāmavarṣī ca parjanyo na ca vyādhibhayaṃ tathā
verses.translation: They were K&sa, Sala and lord Grtsamada. The son of Grtsamada was Sunaka from whom Saunaka was born.
verses.wordMeaning: They were K&sa, Sala and lord Grtsamada. The son of Grtsamada was Sunaka from whom Saunaka was born.
verses.commentary: Sense: They were K&sa, Sala and lord Grtsamada. The son of Grtsamada was Sunaka from whom Saunaka was born.

verses.sanskrit: लिप्सां चक्रे प्रसेनात्तु मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् । गोविन्दो न च तं लेभे शक्तो ऽपि न जहार च
verses.transliteration: lipsāṃ cakre prasenāttu maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam / govindo na ca taṃ lebhe śakto 'pi na jahāra ca
verses.translation: Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaifyas and Sudras were born in his family, O Brahmanas, on account of their diverse Karmans.
verses.wordMeaning: Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaifyas and Sudras were born in his family, O Brahmanas, on account of their diverse Karmans.
verses.commentary: Sense: Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaifyas and Sudras were born in his family, O Brahmanas, on account of their diverse Karmans.

verses.sanskrit: कधाचिन्मृगयां यातः प्रसेनस्तेन भूषितः । स्यमन्तककृते सिंहाद्वधं प्राप सुदारुणम्
verses.transliteration: kadhācinmṛgayāṃ yātaḥ prasenastena bhūṣitaḥ / syamantakakṛte siṃhādvadhaṃ prāpa sudāruṇam
verses.translation: When the second Dvapara arrived, king Dlrgba- tapas, the ruler of Ka£i, a descendant of Sunahotra being desirous of a son, performed a penance.
verses.wordMeaning: When the second Dvapara arrived, king Dlrgba- tapas, the ruler of Ka£i, a descendant of Sunahotra being desirous of a son, performed a penance.
verses.commentary: Sense: When the second Dvapara arrived, king Dlrgba- tapas, the ruler of Ka£i, a descendant of Sunahotra being desirous of a son, performed a penance.

verses.sanskrit: जांबवानृक्षराजस्तु तं सिंहं निजघान वै । आदाय च मणिं दिव्यं स्वबिलं प्रविवेश ह
verses.transliteration: jāṃbavānṛkṣarājastu taṃ siṃhaṃ nijaghāna vai / ādāya ca maṇiṃ divyaṃ svabilaṃ praviveśa ha
verses.translation: The king desired to propitiate lord Dhanvantari for the sake of a son. Thereupon, Dhanvantari urged the king to choose a boon as he pleased.
verses.wordMeaning: The king desired to propitiate lord Dhanvantari for the sake of a son. Thereupon, Dhanvantari urged the king to choose a boon as he pleased.
verses.commentary: Sense: The king desired to propitiate lord Dhanvantari for the sake of a son. Thereupon, Dhanvantari urged the king to choose a boon as he pleased.

verses.sanskrit: तत्कर्म कृष्णस्य ततो वृष्ण्यन्धकमहत्तराः । मणिं गृध्नोस्तु मन्वानास्तमेव विशशङ्किरे
verses.transliteration: tatkarma kṛṣṇasya tato vṛṣṇyandhakamahattarāḥ / maṇiṃ gṛdhnostu manvānāstameva viśaśaṅkire
verses.translation: "O lord, if you are pleased with. me, be my son,, bestowerof my goal". After saying "So be it", the lord vanished there itself.
verses.wordMeaning: "O lord, if you are pleased with. me, be my son,, bestowerof my goal". After saying "So be it", the lord vanished there itself.
verses.commentary: Sense: "O lord, if you are pleased with. me, be my son,, bestowerof my goal". After saying "So be it", the lord vanished there itself.

verses.sanskrit: मिथ्यापवादं तेभ्यस्तं बलवानरिसूदनः । अमृष्यमाणो भगवान्वनं स विचचार ह
verses.transliteration: mithyāpavādaṃ tebhyastaṃ balavānarisūdanaḥ / amṛṣyamāṇo bhagavānvanaṃ sa vicacāra ha
verses.translation: The son of Dhanvantari became well known as Ketuman. The son bom to Ketuman became king Bhfmaratha.
verses.wordMeaning: The son of Dhanvantari became well known as Ketuman. The son bom to Ketuman became king Bhfmaratha.
verses.commentary: Sense: The son of Dhanvantari became well known as Ketuman. The son bom to Ketuman became king Bhfmaratha.

verses.sanskrit: स तु प्रोसेनो मृगयामचरद्यत्र चाप्यथ । प्रसेनस्य पदं ग्राह्यं पुरं पौराप्तकारिभिः
verses.transliteration: sa tu proseno mṛgayāmacaradyatra cāpyatha / prasenasya padaṃ grāhyaṃ puraṃ paurāptakāribhiḥ
verses.translation: The son of Bhimaratha became an intelligent lord of the subjects. Well-renowned as Divod&sa,1 he became the lord of Varanasi.
verses.wordMeaning: The son of Bhimaratha became an intelligent lord of the subjects. Well-renowned as Divod&sa,1 he became the lord of Varanasi.
verses.commentary: Sense: The son of Bhimaratha became an intelligent lord of the subjects. Well-renowned as Divod&sa,1 he became the lord of Varanasi.

verses.sanskrit: ऋक्षवन्तं गिरिवरं विन्ध्यं च नगमुत्तमम् । अन्वेषयत्परिश्रान्तः स ददर्श महामनाः
verses.transliteration: ṛkṣavantaṃ girivaraṃ vindhyaṃ ca nagamuttamam / anveṣayatpariśrāntaḥ sa dadarśa mahāmanāḥ
verses.translation: At this time, a Raksasa named Ksemaka, colonised the city of Var&nasi which had been a desolate and tenantless place.
verses.wordMeaning: At this time, a Raksasa named Ksemaka, colonised the city of Var&nasi which had been a desolate and tenantless place.
verses.commentary: Sense: At this time, a Raksasa named Ksemaka, colonised the city of Var&nasi which had been a desolate and tenantless place.

verses.sanskrit: साश्वं हतं प्रसेनं तं नाविन्दत्तत्र वै मणिम् । अथ सिंहः प्रसेनस्य शरीरस्याविदूरतः
verses.transliteration: sāśvaṃ hataṃ prasenaṃ taṃ nāvindattatra vai maṇim / atha siṃhaḥ prasenasya śarīrasyāvidūrataḥ
verses.translation: Earlier, the city had been cursed by the noble-souled Nikumbha, again and again — "This city will be void of people and a deserted place for a thousand years".
verses.wordMeaning: Earlier, the city had been cursed by the noble-souled Nikumbha, again and again — "This city will be void of people and a deserted place for a thousand years".
verses.commentary: Sense: Earlier, the city had been cursed by the noble-souled Nikumbha, again and again — "This city will be void of people and a deserted place for a thousand years".

verses.sanskrit: ऋक्षेण निहतो दृष्टः पदैरृक्षस्य सूचितः । पदैरन्वेषयामास गुहामृक्षस्य यादवः
verses.transliteration: ṛkṣeṇa nihato dṛṣṭaḥ padairṛkṣasya sūcitaḥ / padairanveṣayāmāsa guhāmṛkṣasya yādavaḥ
verses.translation: What for did Nikumbha curse Varanasi formerly? Why did Nikumbha the noble-souled one curse the holy place of the Siddhas?
verses.wordMeaning: What for did Nikumbha curse Varanasi formerly? Why did Nikumbha the noble-souled one curse the holy place of the Siddhas?
verses.commentary: Sense: What for did Nikumbha curse Varanasi formerly? Why did Nikumbha the noble-souled one curse the holy place of the Siddhas?

verses.sanskrit: महत्यन्तर्बिले वाणीं शश्राव प्रमदेरिताम् । धात्र्या कुमारमादाय सुतं जांबवतो द्विजाः । क्रीडयन्त्याथ मणिना मारोदीरित्युदीरितम्
verses.transliteration: mahatyantarbile vāṇīṃ śaśrāva pramaderitām / dhātryā kumāramādāya sutaṃ jāṃbavato dvijāḥ / krīḍayantyātha maṇinā mārodīrityudīritam
verses.translation: The saintly king Divod&sa lived in that flourishing city after obtaining it. The ruler of men of great brilliance lived there in that prosperous city.
verses.wordMeaning: The saintly king Divod&sa lived in that flourishing city after obtaining it. The ruler of men of great brilliance lived there in that prosperous city.
verses.commentary: Sense: The saintly king Divod&sa lived in that flourishing city after obtaining it. The ruler of men of great brilliance lived there in that prosperous city.

verses.sanskrit: धात्र्युवाच प्रसेनमवधीत्सिंहः सिंहो जांबवता हतः
verses.transliteration: dhātryuvāca prasenamavadhītsiṃhaḥ siṃho jāṃbavatā hataḥ
verses.translation: At the behest of the lord, theParisadas (attendants) of various kinds of forms, the ascetics began to delight goddess Umi (MaheSvarl) by adopting the forms and guise as mentioned before.
verses.wordMeaning: At the behest of the lord, theParisadas (attendants) of various kinds of forms, the ascetics began to delight goddess Umi (MaheSvarl) by adopting the forms and guise as mentioned before.
verses.commentary: Sense: At the behest of the lord, theParisadas (attendants) of various kinds of forms, the ascetics began to delight goddess Umi (MaheSvarl) by adopting the forms and guise as mentioned before.

verses.sanskrit: सुकुमारक मारो दीस्तव ह्यें स्यमन्तकः । व्यक्तीकृतश्च शब्दः स तूर्णं चापि ययौ बिलम्
verses.transliteration: sukumāraka māro dīstava hyeṃ syamantakaḥ / vyaktīkṛtaśca śabdaḥ sa tūrṇaṃ cāpi yayau bilam
verses.translation: She said — "Your husband MaheSvara has no manners or good conduct even in my presence. He is always ifidigent in every respect. Alas, he is not ashamed".
verses.wordMeaning: She said — "Your husband MaheSvara has no manners or good conduct even in my presence. He is always ifidigent in every respect. Alas, he is not ashamed".
verses.commentary: Sense: She said — "Your husband MaheSvara has no manners or good conduct even in my presence. He is always ifidigent in every respect. Alas, he is not ashamed".

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यच्च बिलाभ्याशे प्रसेन मवदारितम् । प्रविश्य चापि भगवान्स ऋक्षबिलमञ्जसा
verses.transliteration: apaśyacca bilābhyāśe prasena mavadāritam / praviśya cāpi bhagavānsa ṛkṣabilamañjasā
verses.translation: On being told thus by her mother in so many words, Parvati did not brook it, that being the natural characteristic of women. Smilingly, the goddess who bestowed boons, went near Hara.
verses.wordMeaning: On being told thus by her mother in so many words, Parvati did not brook it, that being the natural characteristic of women. Smilingly, the goddess who bestowed boons, went near Hara.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being told thus by her mother in so many words, Parvati did not brook it, that being the natural characteristic of women. Smilingly, the goddess who bestowed boons, went near Hara.

verses.sanskrit: ददर्श ऋक्षराजानं जांबवन्तमुदारधीः । युयुधे वासुदेवस्तु बिले जांबवता सह
verses.transliteration: dadarśa ṛkṣarājānaṃ jāṃbavantamudāradhīḥ / yuyudhe vāsudevastu bile jāṃbavatā saha
verses.translation: With a sorrowful face, the goddess spoke to Mahadeva — "O lord, I will not stay here, Take me to your abode".
verses.wordMeaning: With a sorrowful face, the goddess spoke to Mahadeva — "O lord, I will not stay here, Take me to your abode".
verses.commentary: Sense: With a sorrowful face, the goddess spoke to Mahadeva — "O lord, I will not stay here, Take me to your abode".

verses.sanskrit: बाहुभ्यामेव गोविन्दो दिवसानेकविंशतिम् । प्रविष्टे च बिलं कृष्णे वसुदेवापुरस्सराः
verses.transliteration: bāhubhyāmeva govindo divasānekaviṃśatim / praviṣṭe ca bilaṃ kṛṣṇe vasudevāpurassarāḥ
verses.translation: On being told thus, Mah&deva examined all the worlds, O excellent Br&hmanas and desired to take up residence on the Earth.
verses.wordMeaning: On being told thus, Mah&deva examined all the worlds, O excellent Br&hmanas and desired to take up residence on the Earth.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being told thus, Mah&deva examined all the worlds, O excellent Br&hmanas and desired to take up residence on the Earth.

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्द्वारवतीं चैत्य हतं कृष्णं न्यवेदयन् । वासुदेवस्तु निर्जित्य जांबवन्तं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration: punardvāravatīṃ caitya hataṃ kṛṣṇaṃ nyavedayan / vāsudevastu nirjitya jāṃbavantaṃ mahābalam
verses.translation: "Since, without any fault on my side, my abode has been destroyed by you, O king, your city shall become a deserted wasteland suddenly".
verses.wordMeaning: "Since, without any fault on my side, my abode has been destroyed by you, O king, your city shall become a deserted wasteland suddenly".
verses.commentary: Sense: "Since, without any fault on my side, my abode has been destroyed by you, O king, your city shall become a deserted wasteland suddenly".

verses.sanskrit: लेभे जांबवन्तीं कन्यामृक्षराजस्य सम्मनाम् । भगवत्तेजसा ग्रस्तो जांबवांन्प्रसभं मणिम्
verses.transliteration: lebhe jāṃbavantīṃ kanyāmṛkṣarājasya sammanām / bhagavattejasā grasto jāṃbavāṃnprasabhaṃ maṇim
verses.translation: Thereupon, on account of that curse, Varanasi be- came a void then. After cursing the city, Nikumbha brought Mahadeva there.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereupon, on account of that curse, Varanasi be- came a void then. After cursing the city, Nikumbha brought Mahadeva there.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thereupon, on account of that curse, Varanasi be- came a void then. After cursing the city, Nikumbha brought Mahadeva there.

verses.sanskrit: सुतां जांबवतीमाशु विष्वक्सेनाय दत्तवान् । मणिं स्यमन्तकं चैव जग्रहात्मविशुद्धये
verses.transliteration: sutāṃ jāṃbavatīmāśu viṣvaksenāya dattavān / maṇiṃ syamantakaṃ caiva jagrahātmaviśuddhaye
verses.translation: Mahadeva of great and noble mind made that deserted vacant city equal to the city of the Devas by means of its wealth and luxury, and made it his abode as well as that of the goddess.
verses.wordMeaning: Mahadeva of great and noble mind made that deserted vacant city equal to the city of the Devas by means of its wealth and luxury, and made it his abode as well as that of the goddess.
verses.commentary: Sense: Mahadeva of great and noble mind made that deserted vacant city equal to the city of the Devas by means of its wealth and luxury, and made it his abode as well as that of the goddess.

verses.sanskrit: अनुनीयर्क्षराजं तं निर्ययौ च तदा बिलात् । एवं स मणिमाहृत्य विशोध्यात्मानमात्मना
verses.transliteration: anunīyarkṣarājaṃ taṃ niryayau ca tadā bilāt / evaṃ sa maṇimāhṛtya viśodhyātmānamātmanā
verses.translation: The goddess sported and diverted her mind there itself. She was wonder-struck at the affluence. For the sake of sports and pastime of the goddess, lord Isana spoke these words: —
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess sported and diverted her mind there itself. She was wonder-struck at the affluence. For the sake of sports and pastime of the goddess, lord Isana spoke these words: —
verses.commentary: Sense: The goddess sported and diverted her mind there itself. She was wonder-struck at the affluence. For the sake of sports and pastime of the goddess, lord Isana spoke these words: —

verses.sanskrit: ददौ सत्राजिते रत्नं मणिं सात्त्वतसन्निधौ । कन्यां पुनर्जांबवतीमुवाह मधुसूदनः
verses.transliteration: dadau satrājite ratnaṃ maṇiṃ sāttvatasannidhau / kanyāṃ punarjāṃbavatīmuvāha madhusūdanaḥ
verses.translation: "I will not leave off my abode. Indeed my abode is Avimukta ". Laughingly he said to her — "My abode is Avimukta. I will not go elsewhere, O gentle lady, after leaving thus.
verses.wordMeaning: "I will not leave off my abode. Indeed my abode is Avimukta ". Laughingly he said to her — "My abode is Avimukta. I will not go elsewhere, O gentle lady, after leaving thus.
verses.commentary: Sense: "I will not leave off my abode. Indeed my abode is Avimukta ". Laughingly he said to her — "My abode is Avimukta. I will not go elsewhere, O gentle lady, after leaving thus.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मान्मिथ्याभिशापात्तु व्यशुध्यन्मधुसूदनः । इमां मिथ्याभिशप्तिं यः कृष्णस्येह व्यपोहिताम्
verses.transliteration: tasmānmithyābhiśāpāttu vyaśudhyanmadhusūdanaḥ / imāṃ mithyābhiśaptiṃ yaḥ kṛṣṇasyeha vyapohitām
verses.translation: Sport along with me in this holy spot, O resplendent lady who has no one superior to you". Hence that (holy place) was called Avimukta by the lord himself.
verses.wordMeaning: Sport along with me in this holy spot, O resplendent lady who has no one superior to you". Hence that (holy place) was called Avimukta by the lord himself.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sport along with me in this holy spot, O resplendent lady who has no one superior to you". Hence that (holy place) was called Avimukta by the lord himself.

verses.sanskrit: वेद मिथ्याभिशप्तिं स नाभिस्पृशति कर्हिचित् । दश त्वासन्सत्रजितो भार्यास्तस्यायुतं सुताः
verses.transliteration: veda mithyābhiśaptiṃ sa nābhispṛśati karhicit / daśa tvāsansatrajito bhāryāstasyāyutaṃ sutāḥ
verses.translation: King Divodasa colonized it after killing a hundred sons of Bhadrasena, who were excellent wielders of bows.
verses.wordMeaning: King Divodasa colonized it after killing a hundred sons of Bhadrasena, who were excellent wielders of bows.
verses.commentary: Sense: King Divodasa colonized it after killing a hundred sons of Bhadrasena, who were excellent wielders of bows.

verses.sanskrit: ख्यातिमन्तस्त्रयस्तेषां भङ्गकारस्तु पूर्वजः । वीरो वातपतिश्चैव तपस्वी च बहुप्रियः
verses.transliteration: khyātimantastrayasteṣāṃ bhaṅgakārastu pūrvajaḥ / vīro vātapatiścaiva tapasvī ca bahupriyaḥ
verses.translation: Pratardana had two sons, Vatsa and Garga who be- came very famous. Alarka was the son of Vatsa anfl Sannati was his son.
verses.wordMeaning: Pratardana had two sons, Vatsa and Garga who be- came very famous. Alarka was the son of Vatsa anfl Sannati was his son.
verses.commentary: Sense: Pratardana had two sons, Vatsa and Garga who be- came very famous. Alarka was the son of Vatsa anfl Sannati was his son.

verses.sanskrit: अथ वीरमती नाम भङ्गकारस्य तु प्रसूः । सुषुवे सा कुमारीस्तु तिस्रो रूपगुणान्विताः
verses.transliteration: atha vīramatī nāma bhaṅgakārasya tu prasūḥ / suṣuve sā kumārīstu tisro rūpaguṇānvitāḥ
verses.translation: At the end of the period of curse, the king of powerful and great arms killed the demon Ksemaka and got rehabilitated the city of Varanasi.
verses.wordMeaning: At the end of the period of curse, the king of powerful and great arms killed the demon Ksemaka and got rehabilitated the city of Varanasi.
verses.commentary: Sense: At the end of the period of curse, the king of powerful and great arms killed the demon Ksemaka and got rehabilitated the city of Varanasi.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यभामोत्तमा स्त्रीणां व्रतिनी च दृढव्रता । तथा तपस्विनी चैव पिता कृष्णय तां ददौ
verses.transliteration: satyabhāmottamā strīṇāṃ vratinī ca dṛḍhavratā / tathā tapasvinī caiva pitā kṛṣṇaya tāṃ dadau
verses.translation: Recorded as Bhatga in AIHT, The line is shown to have dosed there, but our text records GargabhOmi as the son of G&rgya (W. 78-79).
verses.wordMeaning: Recorded as Bhatga in AIHT, The line is shown to have dosed there, but our text records GargabhOmi as the son of G&rgya (W. 78-79).
verses.commentary: Sense: Recorded as Bhatga in AIHT, The line is shown to have dosed there, but our text records GargabhOmi as the son of G&rgya (W. 78-79).

verses.sanskrit: न च सत्राजितः कृष्णो मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् । आदत्त तदुपश्रुत्य भोजेन शतधन्वना
verses.transliteration: na ca satrājitaḥ kṛṣṇo maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam / ādatta tadupaśrutya bhojena śatadhanvanā
verses.translation: The heroic Raji had five hundred sons. This group of Ksatriyas is well known as Rajeya on the Earth. Indra was afraid of them.
verses.wordMeaning: The heroic Raji had five hundred sons. This group of Ksatriyas is well known as Rajeya on the Earth. Indra was afraid of them.
verses.commentary: Sense: The heroic Raji had five hundred sons. This group of Ksatriyas is well known as Rajeya on the Earth. Indra was afraid of them.

verses.sanskrit: तदा हि प्रार्थयामास सत्यभामामनिन्दिताम् । अक्रूरो धनमन्विच्छन्मणिं चैव स्यमन्तकम्
verses.transliteration: tadā hi prārthayāmāsa satyabhāmāmaninditām / akrūro dhanamanvicchanmaṇiṃ caiva syamantakam
verses.translation: At that time a very terrible battle between the Devas and the Asuras took place, when the Devas and the Asuras asked Brahma.
verses.wordMeaning: At that time a very terrible battle between the Devas and the Asuras took place, when the Devas and the Asuras asked Brahma.
verses.commentary: Sense: At that time a very terrible battle between the Devas and the Asuras took place, when the Devas and the Asuras asked Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: सत्राजितं ततो इत्वा शतधन्वा महाबलः । रात्रौ तं मणिमादाय ततो ऽक्रूराय दत्तवान्
verses.transliteration: satrājitaṃ tato itvā śatadhanvā mahābalaḥ / rātrau taṃ maṇimādāya tato 'krūrāya dattavān
verses.translation: "Who will be victorious, O holy lord in the battle between us? Tell us, O lord of all worlds. We wish to hear.*'
verses.wordMeaning: "Who will be victorious, O holy lord in the battle between us? Tell us, O lord of all worlds. We wish to hear.*'
verses.commentary: Sense: "Who will be victorious, O holy lord in the battle between us? Tell us, O lord of all worlds. We wish to hear.*'

verses.sanskrit: अक्रूरस्तु तदा रत्नमादाय स नरर्षभः । समयं कारयाञ्चक्रे बोध्यो नान्यस्य चेत्युत
verses.transliteration: akrūrastu tadā ratnamādāya sa nararṣabhaḥ / samayaṃ kārayāñcakre bodhyo nānyasya cetyuta
verses.translation: "There is no doubt that those, on whose behalf Lord Raji will take up his arms and fight, will conquer the three worlds.1
verses.wordMeaning: "There is no doubt that those, on whose behalf Lord Raji will take up his arms and fight, will conquer the three worlds.1
verses.commentary: Sense: "There is no doubt that those, on whose behalf Lord Raji will take up his arms and fight, will conquer the three worlds.1

verses.sanskrit: वयमभ्युपयोत्स्यामः कृष्णेन त्वां प्रधर्षितम् । मम वै द्वारका सर्वा वेशे तिष्ठत्य संशयम्
verses.transliteration: vayamabhyupayotsyāmaḥ kṛṣṇena tvāṃ pradharṣitam / mama vai dvārakā sarvā veśe tiṣṭhatya saṃśayam
verses.translation: "I shall defeat, O Daityas, the Devas with Indra at their head I shall become Indra with a virtuous soul. Therefore, I shall fight in the battle-field.
verses.wordMeaning: "I shall defeat, O Daityas, the Devas with Indra at their head I shall become Indra with a virtuous soul. Therefore, I shall fight in the battle-field.
verses.commentary: Sense: "I shall defeat, O Daityas, the Devas with Indra at their head I shall become Indra with a virtuous soul. Therefore, I shall fight in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: हते पितरि दुःखार्त्ता सत्यभामा यशस्विनी । प्रययौ रथमारुह्य नगरं वारणावतम्
verses.transliteration: hate pitari duḥkhārttā satyabhāmā yaśasvinī / prayayau rathamāruhya nagaraṃ vāraṇāvatam
verses.translation: If anyone were to listen and narrate the details of dethronement and re-establishment of Indra, he shall never attain the state of wretchedness.
verses.wordMeaning: If anyone were to listen and narrate the details of dethronement and re-establishment of Indra, he shall never attain the state of wretchedness.
verses.commentary: Sense: If anyone were to listen and narrate the details of dethronement and re-establishment of Indra, he shall never attain the state of wretchedness.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यभामा तु तद्वृत्तं भोजस्य शतधन्वनः । भर्तुर्निवेद्य दुःखार्त्ता पार्श्वस्थाश्रूण्यवर्त्तयत्
verses.transliteration: satyabhāmā tu tadvṛttaṃ bhojasya śatadhanvanaḥ / bharturnivedya duḥkhārttā pārśvasthāśrūṇyavarttayat
verses.translation: That lord of subjects desirous of cooked food, per- formed the sacrifice Marutsoma. That king of great splendour performed it every month for sixty years.
verses.wordMeaning: That lord of subjects desirous of cooked food, per- formed the sacrifice Marutsoma. That king of great splendour performed it every month for sixty years.
verses.commentary: Sense: That lord of subjects desirous of cooked food, per- formed the sacrifice Marutsoma. That king of great splendour performed it every month for sixty years.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवानां तु दग्धानां हरिः कृत्वोदकक्रियाम् । कल्यार्थे चैव भ्रातॄणां न्ययोजयत सात्यकिम्
verses.transliteration: pāṇḍavānāṃ tu dagdhānāṃ hariḥ kṛtvodakakriyām / kalyārthe caiva bhrātṝṇāṃ nyayojayata sātyakim
verses.translation: The gods, Maruts, were pleased by the sacrifice Marut- soma of that king. Delighted in their heart, they give never- failing cooked food with all the other articles he should desire.
verses.wordMeaning: The gods, Maruts, were pleased by the sacrifice Marut- soma of that king. Delighted in their heart, they give never- failing cooked food with all the other articles he should desire.
verses.commentary: Sense: The gods, Maruts, were pleased by the sacrifice Marut- soma of that king. Delighted in their heart, they give never- failing cooked food with all the other articles he should desire.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्वरितमागत्य द्वारकां मधुसूदनः । पूर्वजं हलिनं श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration: tatastvaritamāgatya dvārakāṃ madhusūdanaḥ / pūrvajaṃ halinaṃ śrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt
verses.translation: VV. 1-6 speak of Maruta and Mitra-Jyoti. But these have no connection with any dynasty in this chapter.
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 1-6 speak of Maruta and Mitra-Jyoti. But these have no connection with any dynasty in this chapter.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 1-6 speak of Maruta and Mitra-Jyoti. But these have no connection with any dynasty in this chapter.

verses.sanskrit: हतः प्रसेनः सिंहेन सत्राजिच्छतधन्वना । स्यमन्तको मार्गणीयस्तस्य प्रभुरहं प्रभो
verses.transliteration: hataḥ prasenaḥ siṃhena satrājicchatadhanvanā / syamantako mārgaṇīyastasya prabhurahaṃ prabho
verses.translation: His food taken in once did not get wasted for a day
verses.wordMeaning: His food taken in once did not get wasted for a day
verses.commentary: Sense: His food taken in once did not get wasted for a day

verses.sanskrit: तहारोह रथं शीघ्रं भोजं हत्वा महाबलम् । स्यमन्तकं महाबाहो सामान्यं वो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration: tahāroha rathaṃ śīghraṃ bhojaṃ hatvā mahābalam / syamantakaṃ mahābāho sāmānyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: To the daughter of Mitra-jyoti and the intelligent Maruta were bom many sons who were conversant with dharma, could realize salvation and who were endowed with great intrinsic strength.
verses.wordMeaning: To the daughter of Mitra-jyoti and the intelligent Maruta were bom many sons who were conversant with dharma, could realize salvation and who were endowed with great intrinsic strength.
verses.commentary: Sense: To the daughter of Mitra-jyoti and the intelligent Maruta were bom many sons who were conversant with dharma, could realize salvation and who were endowed with great intrinsic strength.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रवृत्ते युद्धे तु तुमुले भोजकृष्णयोः । शतधन्वा तमक्रूरमवैक्षत्सर्वतो दिशम्
verses.transliteration: tataḥ pravṛtte yuddhe tu tumule bhojakṛṣṇayoḥ / śatadhanvā tamakrūramavaikṣatsarvato diśam
verses.translation: They renounced the rites and vows pertaining to the householder and adopted Vairdgya (non-attachment to worldly desires or objects). After taking up the duties of recluses they attained salvation.
verses.wordMeaning: They renounced the rites and vows pertaining to the householder and adopted Vairdgya (non-attachment to worldly desires or objects). After taking up the duties of recluses they attained salvation.
verses.commentary: Sense: They renounced the rites and vows pertaining to the householder and adopted Vairdgya (non-attachment to worldly desires or objects). After taking up the duties of recluses they attained salvation.

verses.sanskrit: अनालब्धावहारौ तु कृत्वा भोजजनार्द्दनौ । शक्तो ऽपि शाठ्याद्धार्दिक्यो नाक्रूरो ऽभ्युपपद्यत
verses.transliteration: anālabdhāvahārau tu kṛtvā bhojajanārddanau / śakto 'pi śāṭhyāddhārdikyo nākrūro 'bhyupapadyata
verses.translation: Sffijaya, the son of Pratipaksa, became well-known. Jaya was the son of Srfijaya. Vijaya was born to him.
verses.wordMeaning: Sffijaya, the son of Pratipaksa, became well-known. Jaya was the son of Srfijaya. Vijaya was born to him.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sffijaya, the son of Pratipaksa, became well-known. Jaya was the son of Srfijaya. Vijaya was born to him.

verses.sanskrit: अपयोते ततो बुद्धिं भूयश्चक्रे भयान्वितः । योजनानां शतं साग्रं हृदया प्रत्यपद्यत
verses.transliteration: apayote tato buddhiṃ bhūyaścakre bhayānvitaḥ / yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ hṛdayā pratyapadyata
verses.translation: This dynasty of Anenas (also given in V&. 7-11 and Brahma 27-31) was limited and could not be properly located. Bh.P.IX. 17 gives a different line of Anenas.
verses.wordMeaning: This dynasty of Anenas (also given in V&. 7-11 and Brahma 27-31) was limited and could not be properly located. Bh.P.IX. 17 gives a different line of Anenas.
verses.commentary: Sense: This dynasty of Anenas (also given in V&. 7-11 and Brahma 27-31) was limited and could not be properly located. Bh.P.IX. 17 gives a different line of Anenas.

verses.sanskrit: विख्याता हृदया नाम शतयोजनगामिनी । भोजस्य वडवा दिव्या यया कृष्णमयोधयत्
verses.transliteration: vikhyātā hṛdayā nāma śatayojanagāminī / bhojasya vaḍavā divyā yayā kṛṣṇamayodhayat
verses.translation: Yati adopted the path of salvation. He became a sage and became one with Brahman. Among the other five*, it was Yayati who became king.
verses.wordMeaning: Yati adopted the path of salvation. He became a sage and became one with Brahman. Among the other five*, it was Yayati who became king.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yati adopted the path of salvation. He became a sage and became one with Brahman. Among the other five*, it was Yayati who became king.

verses.sanskrit: क्षीणां जवेन त्दृदयामध्वनः शतयोजने । दृष्ट्वा रथस्य तां वृद्धिं शतधन्वा समुद्रवत्
verses.transliteration: kṣīṇāṃ javena tdṛdayāmadhvanaḥ śatayojane / dṛṣṭvā rathasya tāṃ vṛddhiṃ śatadhanvā samudravat
verses.translation: He got Devayani, the daughter of U£anas, and Sarmistha the Asura lady and daughter of Vr$aparvan, as his wives.
verses.wordMeaning: He got Devayani, the daughter of U£anas, and Sarmistha the Asura lady and daughter of Vr$aparvan, as his wives.
verses.commentary: Sense: He got Devayani, the daughter of U£anas, and Sarmistha the Asura lady and daughter of Vr$aparvan, as his wives.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तस्या हयायास्तु श्रमात्खेदाच्च वै द्विजाः । खमुत्पेतुरथ प्राणाः कृष्णो राममथाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration: tatastasyā hayāyāstu śramātkhedācca vai dvijāḥ / khamutpeturatha prāṇāḥ kṛṣṇo rāmamathābravīt
verses.translation: With that pre-eminent chariot* he constantly con- quered the different kingdoms on the earth. Yayati was invin- cible in battle to the Devas* Danavas and human beings.
verses.wordMeaning: With that pre-eminent chariot* he constantly con- quered the different kingdoms on the earth. Yayati was invin- cible in battle to the Devas* Danavas and human beings.
verses.commentary: Sense: With that pre-eminent chariot* he constantly con- quered the different kingdoms on the earth. Yayati was invin- cible in battle to the Devas* Danavas and human beings.

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठस्वेह महाबाहो दृष्टदोषा मया हयी । पद्भ्यां गत्वा हरिष्यामि मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम्
verses.transliteration: tiṣṭhasveha mahābāho dṛṣṭadoṣā mayā hayī / padbhyāṃ gatvā hariṣyāmi maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam
verses.translation: Abandoned (Banished) by the citizens and people of the outlying districts* that king Lohagandhi ran about here and there. He did not get happiness or mental peace anywhere.
verses.wordMeaning: Abandoned (Banished) by the citizens and people of the outlying districts* that king Lohagandhi ran about here and there. He did not get happiness or mental peace anywhere.
verses.commentary: Sense: Abandoned (Banished) by the citizens and people of the outlying districts* that king Lohagandhi ran about here and there. He did not get happiness or mental peace anywhere.

verses.sanskrit: पद्भ्यामेव ततो गत्वा शतधन्वानमच्युतः । मिथिलोपवने तं वै जघान परमास्त्रवित्
verses.transliteration: padbhyāmeva tato gatvā śatadhanvānamacyutaḥ / mithilopavane taṃ vai jaghāna paramāstravit
verses.translation: Distressed with sorrow and misery as he was, he did not get sympathetic understanding from anyone anywhere. Utterly dejected he sought refuge in the sage Saunaka.
verses.wordMeaning: Distressed with sorrow and misery as he was, he did not get sympathetic understanding from anyone anywhere. Utterly dejected he sought refuge in the sage Saunaka.
verses.commentary: Sense: Distressed with sorrow and misery as he was, he did not get sympathetic understanding from anyone anywhere. Utterly dejected he sought refuge in the sage Saunaka.

verses.sanskrit: स्यमन्तकं न चापश्यद्धत्वा भोजं महाबलम् । निवृत्तं चाब्र वीत्कृष्णं रत्नं देहीति लाङ्गली
verses.transliteration: syamantakaṃ na cāpaśyaddhatvā bhojaṃ mahābalam / nivṛttaṃ cābra vītkṛṣṇaṃ ratnaṃ dehīti lāṅgalī
verses.translation: That saintly king Yayaii, the son of Nahusa, attain- ed old age. He then spoke these words to Yadu, his eldest and the most excellent son.
verses.wordMeaning: That saintly king Yayaii, the son of Nahusa, attain- ed old age. He then spoke these words to Yadu, his eldest and the most excellent son.
verses.commentary: Sense: That saintly king Yayaii, the son of Nahusa, attain- ed old age. He then spoke these words to Yadu, his eldest and the most excellent son.

verses.sanskrit: नास्तीति कृष्णश्चोवाच ततो रामो रुषान्वितः । धिक्छब्दपूर्वमसकृत्प्रत्युवाच जनार्द्दनम्
verses.transliteration: nāstīti kṛṣṇaścovāca tato rāmo ruṣānvitaḥ / dhikchabdapūrvamasakṛtpratyuvāca janārddanam
verses.translation: "Dear son, wrinkles, grey hair and other infirmities of old age have overpowered (lit. encircled) me on account of
verses.wordMeaning: "Dear son, wrinkles, grey hair and other infirmities of old age have overpowered (lit. encircled) me on account of
verses.commentary: Sense: "Dear son, wrinkles, grey hair and other infirmities of old age have overpowered (lit. encircled) me on account of

verses.sanskrit: भातृत्वान्मर्षयाम्वेष स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु व्रजाम्यहम् । कृत्यं न मे द्वारकया न त्वया न च वृष्णिभिः
verses.transliteration: bhātṛtvānmarṣayāmveṣa svasti te 'stu vrajāmyaham / kṛtyaṃ na me dvārakayā na tvayā na ca vṛṣṇibhiḥ
verses.translation: O Yadu, accept my sin along with my old age. Accept my old age."
verses.wordMeaning: O Yadu, accept my sin along with my old age. Accept my old age."
verses.commentary: Sense: O Yadu, accept my sin along with my old age. Accept my old age."

verses.sanskrit: प्रविवेश ततो रामो मिथिलामरिमर्द्दनः । सर्वकामैरुपहृतैर्मैथिलेनैव पूजितः
verses.transliteration: praviveśa tato rāmo mithilāmarimarddanaḥ / sarvakāmairupahṛtairmaithilenaiva pūjitaḥ
verses.translation: On being told thus by Yadu, he became extremely furious. (The king) who was the most excellent among the elo- quent ones spoke to the eldest son after censuring him.
verses.wordMeaning: On being told thus by Yadu, he became extremely furious. (The king) who was the most excellent among the elo- quent ones spoke to the eldest son after censuring him.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being told thus by Yadu, he became extremely furious. (The king) who was the most excellent among the elo- quent ones spoke to the eldest son after censuring him.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु बभ्रुर्मतिमतां वरः । नानारूपान्क्रतून्सर्वा नाजहार निरर्गलान्
verses.transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu babhrurmatimatāṃ varaḥ / nānārūpānkratūnsarvā nājahāra nirargalān
verses.translation: "O evil-minded one, what other devout rite do you have for which you disregard me, your preceptor (and father)? What other Asrama (stage of life) can you have?'*
verses.wordMeaning: "O evil-minded one, what other devout rite do you have for which you disregard me, your preceptor (and father)? What other Asrama (stage of life) can you have?'*
verses.commentary: Sense: "O evil-minded one, what other devout rite do you have for which you disregard me, your preceptor (and father)? What other Asrama (stage of life) can you have?'*

verses.sanskrit: दीक्षामयं सकवचं रक्षार्थं प्रविवेश ह । स्यमन्तककृते प्राज्ञो कान्दिनीजो महामनाः
verses.transliteration: dīkṣāmayaṃ sakavacaṃ rakṣārthaṃ praviveśa ha / syamantakakṛte prājño kāndinījo mahāmanāḥ
verses.translation: "An old man cannot drive a chariot or ride a horse. He cannot enjoy women. He has no pleasure. Therefore, I do not desire old age".
verses.wordMeaning: "An old man cannot drive a chariot or ride a horse. He cannot enjoy women. He has no pleasure. Therefore, I do not desire old age".
verses.commentary: Sense: "An old man cannot drive a chariot or ride a horse. He cannot enjoy women. He has no pleasure. Therefore, I do not desire old age".

verses.sanskrit: अकूर यज्ञा इति ते ख्यातास्तस्य महात्मनः । बह्वन्नदक्षिणाः सर्वे सर्वकामप्रदायिनः
verses.transliteration: akūra yajñā iti te khyātāstasya mahātmanaḥ / bahvannadakṣiṇāḥ sarve sarvakāmapradāyinaḥ
verses.translation: "An old man is as weak and feeble as a child. He is always unclean. He does not perform Homa in the sacred fire at the proper time. I do not like that type of old age."
verses.wordMeaning: "An old man is as weak and feeble as a child. He is always unclean. He does not perform Homa in the sacred fire at the proper time. I do not like that type of old age."
verses.commentary: Sense: "An old man is as weak and feeble as a child. He is always unclean. He does not perform Homa in the sacred fire at the proper time. I do not like that type of old age."

verses.sanskrit: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा गत्वाथ मिथिलां प्रभुः । गदाशिक्षां ततो दिव्यां बलभद्रादवाप्तवान्
verses.transliteration: atha duryodhano rājā gatvātha mithilāṃ prabhuḥ / gadāśikṣāṃ tato divyāṃ balabhadrādavāptavān
verses.translation: He delighted his wives by means of all favours desired by them. He made excellent Brahmanas pleased by granting them everything they desired. He pleased guests by means of foodstuffs and beverages and the Vaisyas (the merchant class) by according them benign administration.
verses.wordMeaning: He delighted his wives by means of all favours desired by them. He made excellent Brahmanas pleased by granting them everything they desired. He pleased guests by means of foodstuffs and beverages and the Vaisyas (the merchant class) by according them benign administration.
verses.commentary: Sense: He delighted his wives by means of all favours desired by them. He made excellent Brahmanas pleased by granting them everything they desired. He pleased guests by means of foodstuffs and beverages and the Vaisyas (the merchant class) by according them benign administration.

verses.sanskrit: प्रसाद्य तु ततो रामो वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथैः । आनीतो द्वारकामेव कृष्णेन च महात्मना
verses.transliteration: prasādya tu tato rāmo vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathaiḥ / ānīto dvārakāmeva kṛṣṇena ca mahātmanā
verses.translation: He delighted Sudras by avoiding cruelty and pre- venting their harassment by others. He controlled decoits by giving punishments and restraining them otherwise. He delighted all subjects duly according to the injunctions of dharma.
verses.wordMeaning: He delighted Sudras by avoiding cruelty and pre- venting their harassment by others. He controlled decoits by giving punishments and restraining them otherwise. He delighted all subjects duly according to the injunctions of dharma.
verses.commentary: Sense: He delighted Sudras by avoiding cruelty and pre- venting their harassment by others. He controlled decoits by giving punishments and restraining them otherwise. He delighted all subjects duly according to the injunctions of dharma.

verses.sanskrit: अक्रूरश्चान्धकैः सार्द्धमथायात्पुरुषर्षभः । युद्धे हत्वा तु शत्रुघ्नं सह बन्धुमता बली
verses.transliteration: akrūraścāndhakaiḥ sārddhamathāyātpuruṣarṣabhaḥ / yuddhe hatvā tu śatrughnaṃ saha bandhumatā balī
verses.translation: Yayati protected the kingdom like another Indra.
verses.wordMeaning: Yayati protected the kingdom like another Indra.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yayati protected the kingdom like another Indra.

verses.sanskrit: सुयज्ञतनयायां तु नरायां नरसत्तमौ । भङ्गकारस्य तनयौ विश्रुतौ सुमहाबलौ
verses.transliteration: suyajñatanayāyāṃ tu narāyāṃ narasattamau / bhaṅgakārasya tanayau viśrutau sumahābalau
verses.translation: You may take up the administration of the realm. Indeed, you alone among all the sons carried out my wish in order to please me." King Yayati, the son of Nahusa took back his old age. Puru regained his youthful age.
verses.wordMeaning: You may take up the administration of the realm. Indeed, you alone among all the sons carried out my wish in order to please me." King Yayati, the son of Nahusa took back his old age. Puru regained his youthful age.
verses.commentary: Sense: You may take up the administration of the realm. Indeed, you alone among all the sons carried out my wish in order to please me." King Yayati, the son of Nahusa took back his old age. Puru regained his youthful age.

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञातेंऽधकमुख्यस्य शक्रघ्नो बन्धुमांश्च तौ । वधे च भङ्गकारस्य कृष्णो न प्रीतिमानभूत्
verses.transliteration: jajñāteṃ'dhakamukhyasya śakraghno bandhumāṃśca tau / vadhe ca bhaṅgakārasya kṛṣṇo na prītimānabhūt
verses.translation: The story of Yay&ti requesting his sons to exchange their youth for a period of 1000 years for his old age is given in details in Mbh.Adi. Chs 81 and 85. The immortal verse:
verses.wordMeaning: The story of Yay&ti requesting his sons to exchange their youth for a period of 1000 years for his old age is given in details in Mbh.Adi. Chs 81 and 85. The immortal verse:
verses.commentary: Sense: The story of Yay&ti requesting his sons to exchange their youth for a period of 1000 years for his old age is given in details in Mbh.Adi. Chs 81 and 85. The immortal verse:

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञातिभेदभयाद्भीतस्तमुबेक्षितवानथ । अपयाते ततो ऽक्रूरे नावर्षत्पाकशासनः
verses.transliteration: jñātibhedabhayādbhītastamubekṣitavānatha / apayāte tato 'krūre nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ
verses.translation: VV.77-90 show that kings in ancient India had to seek some sort of public sanction, before appointing a heir apparent to the throne.
verses.wordMeaning: VV.77-90 show that kings in ancient India had to seek some sort of public sanction, before appointing a heir apparent to the throne.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV.77-90 show that kings in ancient India had to seek some sort of public sanction, before appointing a heir apparent to the throne.

verses.sanskrit: अनावृष्ट्या हतं राष्ट्रमभवद्बहुधा यतः । ततः प्रसादयामासुरक्रूरं कुकुरान्धकाः
verses.transliteration: anāvṛṣṭyā hataṃ rāṣṭramabhavadbahudhā yataḥ / tataḥ prasādayāmāsurakrūraṃ kukurāndhakāḥ
verses.translation: VV.90-94 show that despite the disobedience of his sons Yayati gave parts of his kingdom to his sons, thougn the hereditary throne was given to the youngest son Puru.
verses.wordMeaning: VV.90-94 show that despite the disobedience of his sons Yayati gave parts of his kingdom to his sons, thougn the hereditary throne was given to the youngest son Puru.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV.90-94 show that despite the disobedience of his sons Yayati gave parts of his kingdom to his sons, thougn the hereditary throne was given to the youngest son Puru.

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्द्वारवतीं प्राप्ते तदा दानपतौ तथा । प्रववर्ष सहस्राक्षः कुक्षौ जलनिधेस्ततः
verses.transliteration: punardvāravatīṃ prāpte tadā dānapatau tathā / pravavarṣa sahasrākṣaḥ kukṣau jalanidhestataḥ
verses.translation: The king established the eldest son Yadu in the South-Western quarter. He assigned the Western quarter ta Druhyu and the northern quarter to Anu.
verses.wordMeaning: The king established the eldest son Yadu in the South-Western quarter. He assigned the Western quarter ta Druhyu and the northern quarter to Anu.
verses.commentary: Sense: The king established the eldest son Yadu in the South-Western quarter. He assigned the Western quarter ta Druhyu and the northern quarter to Anu.

verses.sanskrit: कन्यां वै वासुदेवाय स्वसारं शीलसंमताम् । अक्रूरः प्रददौ श्रीमान्प्रीत्यर्थं मुनिपुङ्गवाः
verses.transliteration: kanyāṃ vai vāsudevāya svasāraṃ śīlasaṃmatām / akrūraḥ pradadau śrīmānprītyarthaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ
verses.translation: After conquering the Earth consisting "of seven oceans and continents, King Yayati, the son of Nahusa, divided it into five divisions and distributed them among his sons.
verses.wordMeaning: After conquering the Earth consisting "of seven oceans and continents, King Yayati, the son of Nahusa, divided it into five divisions and distributed them among his sons.
verses.commentary: Sense: After conquering the Earth consisting "of seven oceans and continents, King Yayati, the son of Nahusa, divided it into five divisions and distributed them among his sons.

verses.sanskrit: अथ विज्ञाय योगेन कृष्णो बभ्रुगतं मणिम् । सभामध्ये तदा प्राह तमक्रूरं जनार्द्दनः
verses.transliteration: atha vijñāya yogena kṛṣṇo babhrugataṃ maṇim / sabhāmadhye tadā prāha tamakrūraṃ janārddanaḥ
verses.translation: The entire Earth consisting of towns and seven continents is being protected by them righteously without encroaching on other territories as they were conversant with Dharma.
verses.wordMeaning: The entire Earth consisting of towns and seven continents is being protected by them righteously without encroaching on other territories as they were conversant with Dharma.
verses.commentary: Sense: The entire Earth consisting of towns and seven continents is being protected by them righteously without encroaching on other territories as they were conversant with Dharma.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तद्रत्नं मणिवरं तव हस्तगतं प्रभो । तत्प्रयच्छ स्वमानार्ह मयि मानार्यकं कृथाः
verses.transliteration: yattadratnaṃ maṇivaraṃ tava hastagataṃ prabho / tatprayaccha svamānārha mayi mānāryakaṃ kṛthāḥ
verses.translation: After dividing the Earth among his sons and after transferring the royal glory to his sons, the king, the son of Nahu$a, became delighted.
verses.wordMeaning: After dividing the Earth among his sons and after transferring the royal glory to his sons, the king, the son of Nahu$a, became delighted.
verses.commentary: Sense: After dividing the Earth among his sons and after transferring the royal glory to his sons, the king, the son of Nahu$a, became delighted.

verses.sanskrit: षष्टिवर्षगते काले यद्रोषो ऽभूत्तदा मम । सुसंरूढो ऽसकृत्प्राप्तस्तदा कालात्ययो महान्
verses.transliteration: ṣaṣṭivarṣagate kāle yadroṣo 'bhūttadā mama / susaṃrūḍho 'sakṛtprāptastadā kālātyayo mahān
verses.translation: After laying aside the bow and the arrows, after entrusting the kingdom to his sons and after allotting the duties and responsibilities to his kinsmen, the king became pleased.
verses.wordMeaning: After laying aside the bow and the arrows, after entrusting the kingdom to his sons and after allotting the duties and responsibilities to his kinsmen, the king became pleased.
verses.commentary: Sense: After laying aside the bow and the arrows, after entrusting the kingdom to his sons and after allotting the duties and responsibilities to his kinsmen, the king became pleased.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृष्णस्य वचनात्सर्वसात्त्वतसंसदि । प्रददौ तं मणिं बभ्रुरक्लेशेन महामतिः
verses.transliteration: tataḥ kṛṣṇasya vacanātsarvasāttvatasaṃsadi / pradadau taṃ maṇiṃ babhrurakleśena mahāmatiḥ
verses.translation: In this context the following verses have been formerly sung by Yayati, the great king. By following the advice therein one should restrain and withdraw lustful desires like a tortoise that withdraws his limbs.1
verses.wordMeaning: In this context the following verses have been formerly sung by Yayati, the great king. By following the advice therein one should restrain and withdraw lustful desires like a tortoise that withdraws his limbs.1
verses.commentary: Sense: In this context the following verses have been formerly sung by Yayati, the great king. By following the advice therein one should restrain and withdraw lustful desires like a tortoise that withdraws his limbs.1

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तमार्जवप्राप्तं बभ्रोर्हस्तादरिन्दमः । ददौ हृष्टमनास्तुष्टस्तं मणिं बभ्रवे पुनः
verses.transliteration: tatastamārjavaprāptaṃ babhrorhastādarindamaḥ / dadau hṛṣṭamanāstuṣṭastaṃ maṇiṃ babhrave punaḥ
verses.translation: "Never can lust subside by enjoying the pleasures. Just as the fire is ablaze all the more by ghee offer- ings so also the desires get increased by indulgence.
verses.wordMeaning: "Never can lust subside by enjoying the pleasures. Just as the fire is ablaze all the more by ghee offer- ings so also the desires get increased by indulgence.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Never can lust subside by enjoying the pleasures. Just as the fire is ablaze all the more by ghee offer- ings so also the desires get increased by indulgence.

verses.sanskrit: स कृष्णहस्तात्संप्राप्य मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम् । आबध्य गान्दिनीपुत्रो विरराजांशुमानिव
verses.transliteration: sa kṛṣṇahastātsaṃprāpya maṇiratnaṃ syamantakam / ābadhya gāndinīputro virarājāṃśumāniva
verses.translation: All the food-grains and barleys, all the gold, all the animals and all the women in the world — all these are not sufficient even for one. One who realizes this docs not become deluded.
verses.wordMeaning: All the food-grains and barleys, all the gold, all the animals and all the women in the world — all these are not sufficient even for one. One who realizes this docs not become deluded.
verses.commentary: Sense: All the food-grains and barleys, all the gold, all the animals and all the women in the world — all these are not sufficient even for one. One who realizes this docs not become deluded.

verses.sanskrit: इमां मिथ्याभिशाप्तिं यो विशुद्धिमपि चोत्तमाम् । वेद मिथ्याभिशप्तिं स न लभेत कथञ्चन
verses.transliteration: imāṃ mithyābhiśāptiṃ yo viśuddhimapi cottamām / veda mithyābhiśaptiṃ sa na labheta kathañcana
verses.translation: If one has no inauspicious feelings towards all living beings, if one is not ill-disposed towards anyone mentally* verbally or physically, one realizes the Brahman then.
verses.wordMeaning: If one has no inauspicious feelings towards all living beings, if one is not ill-disposed towards anyone mentally* verbally or physically, one realizes the Brahman then.
verses.commentary: Sense: If one has no inauspicious feelings towards all living beings, if one is not ill-disposed towards anyone mentally* verbally or physically, one realizes the Brahman then.

verses.sanskrit: अनमित्राच्छिनिर्जज्ञे कनिष्ठाद्वृष्णिनन्दनात् । सत्यवान्सत्यसंपन्नः सत्यकस्तस्य चात्मजः
verses.transliteration: anamitrācchinirjajñe kaniṣṭhādvṛṣṇinandanāt / satyavānsatyasaṃpannaḥ satyakastasya cātmajaḥ
verses.translation: If one does not terrify others, if one is not afraid of others, if one neither desires nor hates, one realizes the Brahman then.
verses.wordMeaning: If one does not terrify others, if one is not afraid of others, if one neither desires nor hates, one realizes the Brahman then.
verses.commentary: Sense: If one does not terrify others, if one is not afraid of others, if one neither desires nor hates, one realizes the Brahman then.

verses.sanskrit: सात्यकिर्युयुधानश्च तस्य भूतिः सुतो ऽभवत् । भूतेर्युगन्धरः पुत्र इति भौत्यः प्रकीर्त्तितः
verses.transliteration: sātyakiryuyudhānaśca tasya bhūtiḥ suto 'bhavat / bhūteryugandharaḥ putra iti bhautyaḥ prakīrttitaḥ
verses.translation: VV.97-103 are often quoted and have become in a way, immortal' verses.
verses.wordMeaning: VV.97-103 are often quoted and have become in a way, immortal' verses.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV.97-103 are often quoted and have become in a way, immortal' verses.

verses.sanskrit: माड्याः सुतस्य जज्ञे तु सुतो वृष्णिर्युधाजितः । जज्ञाते तनयौ वृष्णेः श्वफल्कश्चित्रकश्च यः
verses.transliteration: māḍyāḥ sutasya jajñe tu suto vṛṣṇiryudhājitaḥ / jajñāte tanayau vṛṣṇeḥ śvaphalkaścitrakaśca yaḥ
verses.translation: Happiness befalls one who eschews Tr$n& (thirst, covetousness) which cannot be got rid of by evil-minded persons, which does not subside even when one becomes old and infirm and which can be considered an ailment that lasts till our vital airs last (or that causes death).
verses.wordMeaning: Happiness befalls one who eschews Tr$n& (thirst, covetousness) which cannot be got rid of by evil-minded persons, which does not subside even when one becomes old and infirm and which can be considered an ailment that lasts till our vital airs last (or that causes death).
verses.commentary: Sense: Happiness befalls one who eschews Tr$n& (thirst, covetousness) which cannot be got rid of by evil-minded persons, which does not subside even when one becomes old and infirm and which can be considered an ailment that lasts till our vital airs last (or that causes death).

verses.sanskrit: श्वफल्कस्तु महाराजो धर्मात्मा यत्र वर्तते । नास्ति व्याधिभयं तत्र न चावृष्टिभयं तथा
verses.transliteration: śvaphalkastu mahārājo dharmātmā yatra vartate / nāsti vyādhibhayaṃ tatra na cāvṛṣṭibhayaṃ tathā
verses.translation: When one becomes old, one's hair become rotten and decayed; when one becomes old, one's teeth decay, but the desire to live and the greediness to earn wealth do not subside even when one becomes old.
verses.wordMeaning: When one becomes old, one's hair become rotten and decayed; when one becomes old, one's teeth decay, but the desire to live and the greediness to earn wealth do not subside even when one becomes old.
verses.commentary: Sense: When one becomes old, one's hair become rotten and decayed; when one becomes old, one's teeth decay, but the desire to live and the greediness to earn wealth do not subside even when one becomes old.

verses.sanskrit: कादाचित्काशिराजस्य विभोस्तु द्विजसत्तमाः । त्रीणि वर्षाणि विषये नावर्षत्पाकशासनः
verses.transliteration: kādācitkāśirājasya vibhostu dvijasattamāḥ / trīṇi varṣāṇi viṣaye nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ
verses.translation: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.wordMeaning: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."
verses.commentary: Sense: The pleasure of love in the world, the great pleasure of heaven, do not deserve to be on a par with a sixteenth part of the pleasure of destruction of covetousness."

verses.sanskrit: स तत्रवासयामास श्वफल्कं परमार्चितम् । श्वफल्कपरिवासेन प्रावर्षत्पाकशासनः
verses.transliteration: sa tatravāsayāmāsa śvaphalkaṃ paramārcitam / śvaphalkaparivāsena prāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ
verses.translation: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.
verses.wordMeaning: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.
verses.commentary: Sense: I shall recount the line of Yadu, the eldest (son of Yayati) of excellent splendour in detail and in the proper order. Even as I recount it, listen and understand.

verses.sanskrit: श्वफल्कः काशिराजस्य सुतां भार्यामविन्दत । गान्दिनींनाम गां सा हि ददौ विप्राय नित्यशः
verses.transliteration: śvaphalkaḥ kāśirājasya sutāṃ bhāryāmavindata / gāndinīṃnāma gāṃ sā hi dadau viprāya nityaśaḥ
verses.translation: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).
verses.wordMeaning: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).
verses.commentary: Sense: A mountain in Nepal on the eastern bank of the Gandak. Here was the hermitage of sage Bhrgu (De. 34).

verses.sanskrit: सा मातुरुदरस्था वै बहून्वर्षशातान्किल । निवसंती न वै जज्ञे गर्भस्थां तां पिताब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration: sā māturudarasthā vai bahūnvarṣaśātānkila / nivasaṃtī na vai jajñe garbhasthāṃ tāṃ pitābravīt
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: जायस्व शीघ्रं भद्रं ते किमर्थं वापि तिष्ठसि । प्रोवाच चैनं गर्भस्था सा कन्या गां दिने दिने
verses.transliteration: jāyasva śīghraṃ bhadraṃ te kimarthaṃ vāpi tiṣṭhasi / provāca cainaṃ garbhasthā sā kanyā gāṃ dine dine
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: यदि दद्यास्ततो गर्भाद्बहिः स्यां हायनैस्त्रिभिः । तथेत्युवाच तां तस्याः पिता काममपूरयत्
verses.transliteration: yadi dadyāstato garbhādbahiḥ syāṃ hāyanaistribhiḥ / tathetyuvāca tāṃ tasyāḥ pitā kāmamapūrayat
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: दाता यज्वा च शुरश्च श्रुतवानतिथिप्रियः । तस्याः पुत्रः स्मृतो ऽक्रूरः श्वाफल्को भूरिदक्षिणः
verses.transliteration: dātā yajvā ca śuraśca śrutavānatithipriyaḥ / tasyāḥ putraḥ smṛto 'krūraḥ śvāphalko bhūridakṣiṇaḥ
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: उपमङ्गुस्तथा मङ्गुर्मृदुरश्चारिमेजयः । गिरिरक्षस्ततो यक्षः शत्रुघ्नो ऽथारिमर्दनः
verses.transliteration: upamaṅgustathā maṅgurmṛduraścārimejayaḥ / girirakṣastato yakṣaḥ śatrughno 'thārimardanaḥ
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मवृद्धः सुकर्मा च गन्धमादस्तथापरः । आवाहप्रतिवाहौ च वसुदेवा वराङ्गना
verses.transliteration: dharmavṛddhaḥ sukarmā ca gandhamādastathāparaḥ / āvāhaprativāhau ca vasudevā varāṅganā
verses.translation: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.wordMeaning: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Yadu had five sons comparable to the sons of the Devas viz. — Sahasrajit the excellent one (or the eldest), Krosfu, Nila, Aftjika and Laghu.

verses.sanskrit: अक्रूरादौग्रसेन्यां तु सुतौ द्वौ कुलनन्दिनौ । देववानुपदेवश्च जज्ञाते देवसंनिभौ
