verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे वंशानुवर्णनं नाम चतुःसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ ७४॥ समाप्तश्चायं तृतीयः पादः अथोत्तरभागप्रारमभः श्रुत्वा पादं तृतीयं तु क्रान्तं सूतेन धीमता । ततश्चतुर्थं पप्रच्छुः पादं वै ऋषिसत्तमाः
verses.transliteration: iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde vaṃśānuvarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 74// samāptaścāyaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ athottarabhāgaprāramabhaḥ śrutvā pādaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu krāntaṃ sūtena dhīmatā / tataścaturthaṃ papracchuḥ pādaṃ vai ṛṣisattamāḥ
verses.translation: After hearing the third Section recounted by the intelligent Suta, the excellent sages asked him about the fourth Pada.
verses.wordMeaning: After hearing the third Section recounted by the intelligent Suta, the excellent sages asked him about the fourth Pada.
verses.commentary: Sense: After hearing the third Section recounted by the intelligent Suta, the excellent sages asked him about the fourth Pada.

verses.sanskrit: पादः क्रान्तस्तृतीयो ऽयमनुषङ्गेण नस्त्वया । चतुर्थं विस्तरात्पादं संहारं पारिकीर्त्तय
verses.transliteration: pādaḥ krāntastṛtīyo 'yamanuṣaṅgeṇa nastvayā / caturthaṃ vistarātpādaṃ saṃhāraṃ pārikīrttaya
verses.translation: "Out of tenderness and affection for us, the third fore-gone Section has been covered by you. Describe in detail the fourth Section called 'annihilation' (Samhdra).
verses.wordMeaning: "Out of tenderness and affection for us, the third fore-gone Section has been covered by you. Describe in detail the fourth Section called 'annihilation' (Samhdra).
verses.commentary: Sense: "Out of tenderness and affection for us, the third fore-gone Section has been covered by you. Describe in detail the fourth Section called 'annihilation' (Samhdra).

verses.sanskrit: मन्वन्तराणि सर्वाणि पूर्वाण्येवापरैः सह । सप्तर्षीणामथैतेषां सांप्रतस्यान्तरे मनोः
verses.transliteration: manvantarāṇi sarvāṇi pūrvāṇyevāparaiḥ saha / saptarṣīṇāmathaiteṣāṃ sāṃpratasyāntare manoḥ
verses.translation: Although the title signifies the 'merger of the entire three worlds in their constituent elements during the period of a complete d ay (i.e. clay and night) of Brahma ( vide VV. 236,237), it contains much more material from the description of future Manus or rather Manu-periods and the ultimate dissolution of everything after god Brahma's 'merger' into the 'equilibrium of three gunas'.
verses.wordMeaning: Although the title signifies the 'merger of the entire three worlds in their constituent elements during the period of a complete d ay (i.e. clay and night) of Brahma ( vide VV. 236,237),…
verses.commentary: Sense: Although the title signifies the 'merger of the entire three worlds in their constituent elements during the period of a complete d ay (i.e. clay and night) of Brahma ( vide VV. 236,237),…

verses.sanskrit: विस्तरावयवं चैव निसर्गस्य महात्मनः । विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च सर्वमेव ब्रवीहि नः
verses.transliteration: vistarāvayavaṃ caiva nisargasya mahātmanaḥ / vistareṇānupūrvyā ca sarvameva bravīhi naḥ
verses.translation: Understand, even as I recount, the summary of the Manvantaras along with the future seven (Manvantaras) a& well as the dissolution of the worlds.
verses.wordMeaning: Understand, even as I recount, the summary of the Manvantaras along with the future seven (Manvantaras) a& well as the dissolution of the worlds.
verses.commentary: Sense: Understand, even as I recount, the summary of the Manvantaras along with the future seven (Manvantaras) a& well as the dissolution of the worlds.

verses.sanskrit: सूत उवाच भवतां कथयिष्यामि सर्वमेतद्यथातथम् । पादं त्विमं ससंहारं चतुर्थं मुनिसत्तमाः
verses.transliteration: sūta uvāca bhavatāṃ kathayiṣyāmi sarvametadyathātatham / pādaṃ tvimaṃ sasaṃhāraṃ caturthaṃ munisattamāḥ
verses.translation: These Manvantaras have been recounted perfectly. The subjects (i.e. creations) in the seven Manvantaras have also been recounted. 1 2 Listen to the brief description of the future Manvantaras from me.
verses.wordMeaning: These Manvantaras have been recounted perfectly. The subjects (i.e. creations) in the seven Manvantaras have also been recounted. 1 2 Listen to the brief description of the future Manvantaras from me.
verses.commentary: Sense: These Manvantaras have been recounted perfectly. The subjects (i.e. creations) in the seven Manvantaras have also been recounted. 1 2 Listen to the brief description of the future Manvantaras from me.

verses.sanskrit: मनोर्वैवस्वतस्येमं सांप्रतस्य महात्मंनः । विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च निसर्गं शृणुत द्विजाः
verses.transliteration: manorvaivasvatasyemaṃ sāṃpratasya mahātmaṃnaḥ / vistareṇānupūrvyā ca nisargaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ
verses.translation: I shall mention the details of Savarna the future Manu and son ofVivasvan (the Sun god). Understand briefly the future (details).
verses.wordMeaning: I shall mention the details of Savarna the future Manu and son ofVivasvan (the Sun god). Understand briefly the future (details).
verses.commentary: Sense: I shall mention the details of Savarna the future Manu and son ofVivasvan (the Sun god). Understand briefly the future (details).

verses.sanskrit: मन्वन्तराणां संक्षेपं भविष्यैः सह सप्तभिः । प्रलयं चैव लोकानां ब्रुवतो मे निबोधत
verses.transliteration: manvantarāṇāṃ saṃkṣepaṃ bhaviṣyaiḥ saha saptabhiḥ / pralayaṃ caiva lokānāṃ bruvato me nibodhata
verses.translation: The twenty Devas of the Sutapa group are: Rtu, Tapa, Sukra, Krti, Nemi, iPrabhakara, Prabhasa,
verses.wordMeaning: The twenty Devas of the Sutapa group are: Rtu, Tapa, Sukra, Krti, Nemi, iPrabhakara, Prabhasa,
verses.commentary: Sense: The twenty Devas of the Sutapa group are: Rtu, Tapa, Sukra, Krti, Nemi, iPrabhakara, Prabhasa,

verses.sanskrit: एतान्युक्तानि वै सम्यक्सप्तसप्तसु वै प्रजाः । मन्वन्तराणि संक्षेपाच्छृणुता नागतानि मे
verses.transliteration: etānyuktāni vai samyaksaptasaptasu vai prajāḥ / manvantarāṇi saṃkṣepācchṛṇutā nāgatāni me
verses.translation: For the general information about Manu-Periods (Manvantaras). aide supra I. ii. 35-150-215, Ibid chapters 36, 37, 38.
verses.wordMeaning: For the general information about Manu-Periods (Manvantaras). aide supra I. ii. 35-150-215, Ibid chapters 36, 37, 38.
verses.commentary: Sense: For the general information about Manu-Periods (Manvantaras). aide supra I. ii. 35-150-215, Ibid chapters 36, 37, 38.

verses.sanskrit: सावर्णस्य प्रवक्ष्यामि मनोर्वैवस्वतस्य ह । भविष्यस्य भविष्यं तु समासात्तन्निबोधत
verses.transliteration: sāvarṇasya pravakṣyāmi manorvaivasvatasya ha / bhaviṣyasya bhaviṣyaṃ tu samāsāttannibodhata
verses.translation: As stated in Bli. P. XII. 7- 15, in every Manu-Period there are five types of officers: (1) Manu, (2) A group of seven sages, (3) A group of gods, (4) Indra or the chief of gods, (5) Sons of Manu. There it some variation in the details of names etc. of these officers in different Puranas. In this Purana also the information about these office-bearers etc. is given in. a rather confusing way that it is somewhat difficult to prepare a tabular statement for each of the Manus with the names of special office-bearers of each category under him even though the information here is more detailed than in other Puranas like VP.
verses.wordMeaning: As stated in Bli. P. XII. 7- 15, in every Manu-Period there are five types of officers: (1) Manu, (2) A group of seven sages, (3) A group of gods, (4) Indra or the chief of gods, (5) Sons of Manu. There it some variation in the details of names etc.…
verses.commentary: Sense: As stated in Bli. P. XII. 7- 15, in every Manu-Period there are five types of officers: (1) Manu, (2) A group of seven sages, (3) A group of gods, (4) Indra or the chief of gods, (5) Sons of Manu. There it some variation in the details of names etc.…

verses.sanskrit: अनागताश्च सप्तैव स्मृतास्त्विह महर्षयः । कौशिको गालवश्चैव जामदग्न्यश्च भार्गवः
verses.transliteration: anāgatāśca saptaiva smṛtāstviha maharṣayaḥ / kauśiko gālavaścaiva jāmadagnyaśca bhārgavaḥ
verses.translation: They will be Virajas, ArvarTvan, Nirmoka and others. 1 shall mention the nine sons in the other Savarna Manvantaras.
verses.wordMeaning: They will be Virajas, ArvarTvan, Nirmoka and others. 1 shall mention the nine sons in the other Savarna Manvantaras.
verses.commentary: Sense: They will be Virajas, ArvarTvan, Nirmoka and others. 1 shall mention the nine sons in the other Savarna Manvantaras.

verses.sanskrit: द्वैपायनो वशिष्टश्च कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा । आत्रेयो दीप्तिमांश्चैव ऋषयशृङ्गस्तु काश्यपः
verses.transliteration: dvaipāyano vaśiṣṭaśca kṛpaḥ śāradvatastathā / ātreyo dīptimāṃścaiva ṛṣayaśṛṅgastu kāśyapaḥ
verses.translation: Other Savarna Manus will be the future sons of Brahma. They are four, endowed with divine visions such as Merusavarni etc. (or from Merusavarni).
verses.wordMeaning: Other Savarna Manus will be the future sons of Brahma. They are four, endowed with divine visions such as Merusavarni etc. (or from Merusavarni).
verses.commentary: Sense: Other Savarna Manus will be the future sons of Brahma. They are four, endowed with divine visions such as Merusavarni etc. (or from Merusavarni).

verses.sanskrit: भरद्वाजस्तथा द्रौणिरश्वत्थामा महायशाः । एते सप्त महात्मानो भविष्याः परमर्षयः । सुतपाश्चामिताभाश्च सुखाश्चैव गणास्त्रयः
verses.transliteration: bharadvājastathā drauṇiraśvatthāmā mahāyaśāḥ / ete sapta mahātmāno bhaviṣyāḥ paramarṣayaḥ / sutapāścāmitābhāśca sukhāścaiva gaṇāstrayaḥ
verses.translation: They are the grandsons of Daksa, the sons of Kriya, his daughter. They have equipped themselves with great power of penance on the ridge of the Meru. They have great prowess.
verses.wordMeaning: They are the grandsons of Daksa, the sons of Kriya, his daughter. They have equipped themselves with great power of penance on the ridge of the Meru. They have great prowess.
verses.commentary: Sense: They are the grandsons of Daksa, the sons of Kriya, his daughter. They have equipped themselves with great power of penance on the ridge of the Meru. They have great prowess.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां गणस्तु देवानामेकैको विंशकः स्मृतः । नामतस्तु प्रवक्ष्यामि निबोधध्वं समाहिताः
verses.transliteration: teṣāṃ gaṇastu devānāmekaiko viṃśakaḥ smṛtaḥ / nāmatastu pravakṣyāmi nibodhadhvaṃ samāhitāḥ
verses.translation: They are begot by Brahma and others as well as by the intelligent Daksa. On passing away, they go over to Maharloka. They will resort to Meru and become the future Manus.
verses.wordMeaning: They are begot by Brahma and others as well as by the intelligent Daksa. On passing away, they go over to Maharloka. They will resort to Meru and become the future Manus.
verses.commentary: Sense: They are begot by Brahma and others as well as by the intelligent Daksa. On passing away, they go over to Maharloka. They will resort to Meru and become the future Manus.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतुस्तपश्च शुक्रश्च कृतिर्नेमिः प्रभाकरः । प्रभासो मासकृद्धर्मस्तेजोरश्मिः क्रतुर्विराट्
verses.transliteration: ṛtustapaśca śukraśca kṛtirnemiḥ prabhākaraḥ / prabhāso māsakṛddharmastejoraśmiḥ kraturvirāṭ
verses.translation: Those persons endowed with dignity and splendour were formerly born in the Caksusa Manvantara. They them- selves will be born in the future Manvantaras.
verses.wordMeaning: Those persons endowed with dignity and splendour were formerly born in the Caksusa Manvantara. They them- selves will be born in the future Manvantaras.
verses.commentary: Sense: Those persons endowed with dignity and splendour were formerly born in the Caksusa Manvantara. They them- selves will be born in the future Manvantaras.

verses.sanskrit: अर्चिष्मान् द्योतनो भानुर्यशः कीर्त्तिर्बुधो धृतिः
verses.transliteration: arciṣmān dyotano bhānuryaśaḥ kīrttirbudho dhṛtiḥ
verses.translation: Of those Manus who arc the grandsons of Pracctasa Daksa, five are named Savarnas and four are born of great sages.
verses.wordMeaning: Of those Manus who arc the grandsons of Pracctasa Daksa, five are named Savarnas and four are born of great sages.
verses.commentary: Sense: Of those Manus who arc the grandsons of Pracctasa Daksa, five are named Savarnas and four are born of great sages.

verses.sanskrit: विंशतिः सुतपा ह्येते नामभिः परिकीर्त्तिताः । प्रभुर्विभुर्विभासश्च जेता हन्ता रिहा ऋतुः
verses.transliteration: viṃśatiḥ sutapā hyete nāmabhiḥ parikīrttitāḥ / prabhurvibhurvibhāsaśca jetā hantā rihā ṛtuḥ
verses.translation: The entire Earth including the cities and
verses.wordMeaning: The entire Earth including the cities and
verses.commentary: Sense: The entire Earth including the cities and

verses.sanskrit: सुमतिः प्रमतिर्दीप्तिः समाख्यातो महो महान् । देही मुनिरिनः पोष्टा समः सत्यश्च विश्रुतः
verses.transliteration: sumatiḥ pramatirdīptiḥ samākhyāto maho mahān / dehī munirinaḥ poṣṭā samaḥ satyaśca viśrutaḥ
verses.translation: Their detailed description along with that of their
verses.wordMeaning: Their detailed description along with that of their
verses.commentary: Sense: Their detailed description along with that of their

verses.sanskrit: इत्येतेह्यमिताभास्तु विंशतिः परिकीर्त्तिताः । दामो दानी ऋतः सोमो वित्तं वैद्यो यमो निधिः
verses.transliteration: ityetehyamitābhāstu viṃśatiḥ parikīrttitāḥ / dāmo dānī ṛtaḥ somo vittaṃ vaidyo yamo nidhiḥ
verses.translation: They hold offices ofauthority in the Manvantaras (only) once.- After the expiry of the tenure of their office they resort to Maharloka.
verses.wordMeaning: They hold offices ofauthority in the Manvantaras (only) once.- After the expiry of the tenure of their office they resort to Maharloka.
verses.commentary: Sense: They hold offices ofauthority in the Manvantaras (only) once.- After the expiry of the tenure of their office they resort to Maharloka.

verses.sanskrit: होमो हव्यं हुतं दानं देयं दाता तपः शमः । ध्रुवं स्थानं विधानं च नियमश्चेति विंशतिः
verses.transliteration: homo havyaṃ hutaṃ dānaṃ deyaṃ dātā tapaḥ śamaḥ / dhruvaṃ sthānaṃ vidhānaṃ ca niyamaśceti viṃśatiḥ
verses.translation: (?) Ofthem six have passed on and the rest are eight in number. The lord Mann reigns by himself in the case of the previous ones as well in the current one
verses.wordMeaning: (?) Ofthem six have passed on and the rest are eight in number. The lord Mann reigns by himself in the case of the previous ones as well in the current one
verses.commentary: Sense: (?) Ofthem six have passed on and the rest are eight in number. The lord Mann reigns by himself in the case of the previous ones as well in the current one

verses.sanskrit: सुखा ह्येते समाख्याताः सावर्ण्ये प्रथर्मेतरे । मारीचस्यैव ते पुत्राः कश्यपस्य महात्मनः
verses.transliteration: sukhā hyete samākhyātāḥ sāvarṇye pratharmetare / mārīcasyaiva te putrāḥ kaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: Their details should be known through the example of creation of Vaivasvata Manu, because all of them are neither inferior nor superior to Vivasvan.
verses.wordMeaning: Their details should be known through the example of creation of Vaivasvata Manu, because all of them are neither inferior nor superior to Vivasvan.
verses.commentary: Sense: Their details should be known through the example of creation of Vaivasvata Manu, because all of them are neither inferior nor superior to Vivasvan.

verses.sanskrit: सांप्रतस्य भविष्यन्ति षष्टिर्देवास्तदन्तरे । सावर्णस्य मनोः पुत्रा भविष्यन्ति नवैव तु
verses.transliteration: sāṃpratasya bhaviṣyanti ṣaṣṭirdevāstadantare / sāvarṇasya manoḥ putrā bhaviṣyanti navaiva tu
verses.translation: Due to the multiplicity of repetitions, I shall not recount the details of the future as well as past Manvantaras.
verses.wordMeaning: Due to the multiplicity of repetitions, I shall not recount the details of the future as well as past Manvantaras.
verses.commentary: Sense: Due to the multiplicity of repetitions, I shall not recount the details of the future as well as past Manvantaras.

verses.sanskrit: विरजाश्चार्वरीवांश्च निर्मोकाद्यास्तथा परे । नव चान्येषु वक्ष्यामि सावर्णेष्वन्तरेषु वै
verses.transliteration: virajāścārvarīvāṃśca nirmokādyāstathā pare / nava cānyeṣu vakṣyāmi sāvarṇeṣvantareṣu vai
verses.translation: Hence the creations in the different families should be understood partially for the realization of their details and proper sequence.
verses.wordMeaning: Hence the creations in the different families should be understood partially for the realization of their details and proper sequence.
verses.commentary: Sense: Hence the creations in the different families should be understood partially for the realization of their details and proper sequence.

verses.sanskrit: सावर्णमनवश्चान्ये भविष्या ब्रह्मणः सुताः । मेरुसावर्णितस्ते वै चत्वारो दिव्यदृष्टयः
verses.transliteration: sāvarṇamanavaścānye bhaviṣyā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ / merusāvarṇitaste vai catvāro divyadṛṣṭayaḥ
verses.translation: The father took his daughter of Brahma. Vairaja (i.e. Brahma), was seated there attended uponby Dharma and Bhava.
verses.wordMeaning: The father took his daughter of Brahma. Vairaja (i.e. Brahma), was seated there attended uponby Dharma and Bhava.
verses.commentary: Sense: The father took his daughter of Brahma. Vairaja (i.e. Brahma), was seated there attended uponby Dharma and Bhava.

verses.sanskrit: दक्षस्य ते हि वौहित्राः क्रियाया दुहितुः सुताः । महता तपसा युक्ता मेरुपृष्ठे महौ जसः
verses.transliteration: dakṣasya te hi vauhitrāḥ kriyāyā duhituḥ sutāḥ / mahatā tapasā yuktā merupṛṣṭhe mahau jasaḥ
verses.translation: Brahma spoke to Daksa who was seated near Bhava and Dharma. This, your daughter Suvrata, will pro- create four sons who will be splendid Manus establishing the discipline of the. four castes.
verses.wordMeaning: Brahma spoke to Daksa who was seated near Bhava and Dharma. This, your daughter Suvrata, will pro- create four sons who will be splendid Manus establishing the discipline of the. four castes.
verses.commentary: Sense: Brahma spoke to Daksa who was seated near Bhava and Dharma. This, your daughter Suvrata, will pro- create four sons who will be splendid Manus establishing the discipline of the. four castes.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मादिभिस्तेजनिता दक्षेणैव च धीमता । महर्लोकं गता वृत्ता भविष्या मेरुमाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration: brahmādibhistejanitā dakṣeṇaiva ca dhīmatā / maharlokaṃ gatā vṛttā bhaviṣyā merumāśritāḥ
verses.translation: Aisvara, Vaku, Varhsa, Rahu and (the othereight) Grahas (planets) should be known as Paras. Understand the others.
verses.wordMeaning: Aisvara, Vaku, Varhsa, Rahu and (the othereight) Grahas (planets) should be known as Paras. Understand the others.
verses.commentary: Sense: Aisvara, Vaku, Varhsa, Rahu and (the othereight) Grahas (planets) should be known as Paras. Understand the others.

verses.sanskrit: महानुभावास्ते पूर्वं जज्ञिरे चाक्षुषेन्तरे । जज्ञिरे मनवस्ते हि भविष्यानागतान्तरे
verses.transliteration: mahānubhāvāste pūrvaṃ jajñire cākṣuṣentare / jajñire manavaste hi bhaviṣyānāgatāntare
verses.translation: This (Adbhuta) is Skanda, the son of Parvatl (otherwise known as) Karttikeya and Pavaki. The seven sages in the Rohita Manvantara are Medhatithi of the family of
verses.wordMeaning: This (Adbhuta) is Skanda, the son of Parvatl (otherwise known as) Karttikeya and Pavaki. The seven sages in the Rohita Manvantara are Medhatithi of the family of
verses.commentary: Sense: This (Adbhuta) is Skanda, the son of Parvatl (otherwise known as) Karttikeya and Pavaki. The seven sages in the Rohita Manvantara are Medhatithi of the family of

verses.sanskrit: प्राचेतसस्य दक्षस्य दौहित्रा मनवस्तु ये । सावर्णा नामतः पञ्च चत्वारः परमर्षिजाः
verses.transliteration: prācetasasya dakṣasya dauhitrā manavastu ye / sāvarṇā nāmataḥ pañca catvāraḥ paramarṣijāḥ
verses.translation: VV. 55-65 give details of the office-bearers, gods, sages etc. of Meru-Savarni who is otherwise known as Daksa-Savarni. Cf. VP. III. 2. 20-23. Our text gives more detailed information about these categories or groups of office-bearers than in VP.
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 55-65 give details of the office-bearers, gods, sages etc. of Meru-Savarni who is otherwise known as Daksa-Savarni. Cf. VP. III. 2. 20-23. Our text gives more detailed information about these categories or groups of office-bearers than in VP.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 55-65 give details of the office-bearers, gods, sages etc. of Meru-Savarni who is otherwise known as Daksa-Savarni. Cf. VP. III. 2. 20-23. Our text gives more detailed information about these categories or groups of office-bearers than in VP.

verses.sanskrit: संज्ञापुत्रस्तु सावर्णिरेको वैवस्वतस्तथा । ज्येष्ठः संज्ञासुतो नाम मुर्वैवस्वतः प्रभुः
verses.transliteration: saṃjñāputrastu sāvarṇireko vaivasvatastathā / jyeṣṭhaḥ saṃjñāsuto nāma murvaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ
verses.translation: Their Indra, it is said, will be the future
verses.wordMeaning: Their Indra, it is said, will be the future
verses.commentary: Sense: Their Indra, it is said, will be the future

verses.sanskrit: वैवस्वतेंऽतरे प्राप्ते समुत्पत्तिस्तयोः शुभा । चतुर्दशैते मनवः कीर्तिता कीर्तिवर्द्धनाः
verses.transliteration: vaivasvateṃ'tare prāpte samutpattistayoḥ śubhā / caturdaśaite manavaḥ kīrtitā kīrtivarddhanāḥ
verses.translation: Although the specific name of this second Savarni is not mentioned here, it is Brahma-savarni. vide verse 81 below. VV. 66-81 stale the names of groups of gods, sages etc. during this tenth Manu Period. In V. 81 this.Manu is called Prajapatya (i.e. Brahma-savarna).
verses.wordMeaning: Although the specific name of this second Savarni is not mentioned here, it is Brahma-savarni. vide verse 81 below. VV. 66-81 stale the names of groups of gods, sages etc. during this tenth Manu Period. In V. 81 this.Manu is called Prajapatya (i.e. Brahma-savarna).
verses.commentary: Sense: Although the specific name of this second Savarni is not mentioned here, it is Brahma-savarni. vide verse 81 below. VV. 66-81 stale the names of groups of gods, sages etc. during this tenth Manu Period. In V. 81 this.Manu is called Prajapatya (i.e. Brahma-savarna).

verses.sanskrit: वेदे स्मृतौ पुराणे च सर्वे ते प्रभविष्णवः । प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे भूतानां पतयः स्थिताः
verses.transliteration: vede smṛtau purāṇe ca sarve te prabhaviṣṇavaḥ / prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve bhūtānāṃ patayaḥ sthitāḥ
verses.translation: These are remembered as the future mental sons of Brahma. Their Indra is Vrsa by name. He will be the future king of Suras.
verses.wordMeaning: These are remembered as the future mental sons of Brahma. Their Indra is Vrsa by name. He will be the future king of Suras.
verses.commentary: Sense: These are remembered as the future mental sons of Brahma. Their Indra is Vrsa by name. He will be the future king of Suras.

verses.sanskrit: तैरियं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना । पूर्णं युगसहस्रं वै परिपाल्या नरेश्वरैः
verses.transliteration: tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā / pūrṇaṃ yugasahasraṃ vai paripālyā nareśvaraiḥ
verses.translation: In the twelfth Manvantara Marni will be Rudra's son. The fourth Savarna will be Rudrasavarna. 1 Listen to the Devas during his Manvantara.
verses.wordMeaning: In the twelfth Manvantara Marni will be Rudra's son. The fourth Savarna will be Rudrasavarna. 1 Listen to the Devas during his Manvantara.
verses.commentary: Sense: In the twelfth Manvantara Marni will be Rudra's son. The fourth Savarna will be Rudrasavarna. 1 Listen to the Devas during his Manvantara.

verses.sanskrit: प्रजाभिस्तपसा चैव विस्तरस्तेषु वक्ष्यते । चतुर्द्दशैते विज्ञेयाः सर्गाः स्वायंभुवादयः
verses.transliteration: prajābhistapasā caiva vistarasteṣu vakṣyate / caturddaśaite vijñeyāḥ sargāḥ svāyaṃbhuvādayaḥ
verses.translation: The future Devas (of this Manvantara) are- said to be of five groups. They are Haritas, Rohitas, Sumanas, Sukarmans and Sutaras.
verses.wordMeaning: The future Devas (of this Manvantara) are- said to be of five groups. They are Haritas, Rohitas, Sumanas, Sukarmans and Sutaras.
verses.commentary: Sense: The future Devas (of this Manvantara) are- said to be of five groups. They are Haritas, Rohitas, Sumanas, Sukarmans and Sutaras.

verses.sanskrit: मन्वन्तराधिकारेषु वर्त्तन्ते ऽत्र सकृत्सकृत् । विनिवृत्ताधिकारास्ते महार्लोकं समाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration: manvantarādhikāreṣu varttante 'tra sakṛtsakṛt / vinivṛttādhikārāste mahārlokaṃ samāśritāḥ
verses.translation: Those thirty-three Devas who have already been mentioned, beginning with Tusita, should be known as Sumanas.
verses.wordMeaning: Those thirty-three Devas who have already been mentioned, beginning with Tusita, should be known as Sumanas.
verses.commentary: Sense: Those thirty-three Devas who have already been mentioned, beginning with Tusita, should be known as Sumanas.

verses.sanskrit: समतीतास्तु ये तेषामष्टौ षट् च तथापरे । पूर्वेषु सांप्रतश्चायं शास्ति वैवस्वतः प्रभुः
verses.transliteration: samatītāstu ye teṣāmaṣṭau ṣaṭ ca tathāpare / pūrveṣu sāṃprataścāyaṃ śāsti vaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ
verses.translation: The following are the sons of the twelfth Manu viz. — Devavan, Upadeva, Devas re stha, Vidhuratha, Mitravan, Mitrasena, Citrasena, Amitraha, Mitrabahu and Suvarcas.
verses.wordMeaning: The following are the sons of the twelfth Manu viz. — Devavan, Upadeva, Devas re stha, Vidhuratha, Mitravan, Mitrasena, Citrasena, Amitraha, Mitrabahu and Suvarcas.
verses.commentary: Sense: The following are the sons of the twelfth Manu viz. — Devavan, Upadeva, Devas re stha, Vidhuratha, Mitravan, Mitrasena, Citrasena, Amitraha, Mitrabahu and Suvarcas.

verses.sanskrit: ये शिष्टास्तान्प्रवक्ष्यामि सह देवर्षिदानवैः । सह प्रजा निसर्गेण सर्वांस्ते ऽनागतान्द्विजः
verses.transliteration: ye śiṣṭāstānpravakṣyāmi saha devarṣidānavaiḥ / saha prajā nisargeṇa sarvāṃste 'nāgatāndvijaḥ
verses.translation: Divaspati of great inherent prowess will become their Indra. The sons ofthe son ofPulaha should be known as Ruci's sons.
verses.wordMeaning: Divaspati of great inherent prowess will become their Indra. The sons ofthe son ofPulaha should be known as Ruci's sons.
verses.commentary: Sense: Divaspati of great inherent prowess will become their Indra. The sons ofthe son ofPulaha should be known as Ruci's sons.

verses.sanskrit: वैवस्वत निसर्गेण तेषां ज्ञेयस्तु विस्तरः । अनूना नातिरिक्तास्ते यस्मात्मर्वे विवस्वतः
verses.transliteration: vaivasvata nisargeṇa teṣāṃ jñeyastu vistaraḥ / anūnā nātiriktāste yasmātmarve vivasvataḥ
verses.translation: In the thirteenth Manvantara, the following will be the sons of Manu Raucya. They will be ten (in number). Theyare Gitra-Sena, Vicitra, Naya, Dharma, Dhrta, Bhava, Aneka, Ksatraviddha, Surasa and Nirbhaya.
verses.wordMeaning: In the thirteenth Manvantara, the following will be the sons of Manu Raucya. They will be ten (in number). Theyare Gitra-Sena, Vicitra, Naya, Dharma, Dhrta, Bhava, Aneka, Ksatraviddha, Surasa and Nirbhaya.
verses.commentary: Sense: In the thirteenth Manvantara, the following will be the sons of Manu Raucya. They will be ten (in number). Theyare Gitra-Sena, Vicitra, Naya, Dharma, Dhrta, Bhava, Aneka, Ksatraviddha, Surasa and Nirbhaya.

verses.sanskrit: पुनरुक्तबहुत्वात्तु न वक्ष्ये तेषु विस्तरम् । मन्वन्तरेषु भाव्येषु भूतेष्वपि तथैव च
verses.transliteration: punaruktabahutvāttu na vakṣye teṣu vistaram / manvantareṣu bhāvyeṣu bhūteṣvapi tathaiva ca
verses.translation: VV. 106-116 state the office-bearers in the regime of the last Manu Bhautya. Our text omits the nameoflndra of this Manvantara. VP. III. 2. 41 informs us that Suci was the Indra then. He seems to be different from Suci, the son of this Manu (in V. 114).
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 106-116 state the office-bearers in the regime of the last Manu Bhautya. Our text omits the nameoflndra of this Manvantara. VP. III. 2. 41 informs us that Suci was the Indra then. He seems to be different from Suci, the son of this Manu (in V. 114).
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 106-116 state the office-bearers in the regime of the last Manu Bhautya. Our text omits the nameoflndra of this Manvantara. VP. III. 2. 41 informs us that Suci was the Indra then. He seems to be different from Suci, the son of this Manu (in V. 114).

verses.sanskrit: कुलेकुले निसर्गास्तु तस्माज्ज्ञेया विभागशः । तेषामेव हि सिद्ध्यर्थं विस्तरेण क्रमेण च
verses.transliteration: kulekule nisargāstu tasmājjñeyā vibhāgaśaḥ / teṣāmeva hi siddhyarthaṃ vistareṇa krameṇa ca
verses.translation: After withdrawing (i.e. annihilating) gods, sages, PTtrs and Danavas (demons), god Brahma, on visualizing the end ofhis day at the end of Yuga, verily puts an end to his creation.
verses.wordMeaning: After withdrawing (i.e. annihilating) gods, sages, PTtrs and Danavas (demons), god Brahma, on visualizing the end ofhis day at the end of Yuga, verily puts an end to his creation.
verses.commentary: Sense: After withdrawing (i.e. annihilating) gods, sages, PTtrs and Danavas (demons), god Brahma, on visualizing the end ofhis day at the end of Yuga, verily puts an end to his creation.

verses.sanskrit: दक्षस्य कन्या धर्मिष्ठा सुव्रता नाम विश्रुता । सर्वकन्यावरिष्ठा तु ज्येष्ठा या वीरिणीसुता
verses.transliteration: dakṣasya kanyā dharmiṣṭhā suvratā nāma viśrutā / sarvakanyāvariṣṭhā tu jyeṣṭhā yā vīriṇīsutā
verses.translation: Persons who know that the day of god Brahma terminates at the end of a thousand sets offour Yugas and that his night ends with a thousand sots of four Yugas are called the conversant ones with the day and night (of god-Brahma).
verses.wordMeaning: Persons who know that the day of god Brahma terminates at the end of a thousand sets offour Yugas and that his night ends with a thousand sots of four Yugas are called the conversant ones with the day and night (of god-Brahma).
verses.commentary: Sense: Persons who know that the day of god Brahma terminates at the end of a thousand sets offour Yugas and that his night ends with a thousand sots of four Yugas are called the conversant ones with the day and night (of god-Brahma).

verses.sanskrit: गृहीत्वा तां पिता कन्यां जगाम ब्रह्मणो ऽतिके । वैराजस्थमुपासीनं धर्मेण च भवेन च
verses.transliteration: gṛhītvā tāṃ pitā kanyāṃ jagāma brahmaṇo 'tike / vairājasthamupāsīnaṃ dharmeṇa ca bhavena ca
verses.translation: The Pratisaficara (Dissolution awd reabsorption) of all living beings is of three types viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and the Atyantika (the ultimate one).
verses.wordMeaning: The Pratisaficara (Dissolution awd reabsorption) of all living beings is of three types viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and the Atyantika (the ultimate one).
verses.commentary: Sense: The Pratisaficara (Dissolution awd reabsorption) of all living beings is of three types viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and the Atyantika (the ultimate one).

verses.sanskrit: भवधर्मसमीपस्थं दक्षं ब्रह्माभ्यभाषत । दक्ष कन्या तवेयं वै जनयिष्यति सुव्रता
verses.transliteration: bhavadharmasamīpasthaṃ dakṣaṃ brahmābhyabhāṣata / dakṣa kanyā taveyaṃ vai janayiṣyati suvratā
verses.translation: After stating what happens after the day of god Brahma is over, the author explains the three types of dissolutions viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and Atyantika (The Ultimate one, resulting from spiritual knowledge) vide VV. 128-132.
verses.wordMeaning: After stating what happens after the day of god Brahma is over, the author explains the three types of dissolutions viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and Atyantika (The Ultimate one, resulting from spiritual knowledge) vide VV. 128-132.
verses.commentary: Sense: After stating what happens after the day of god Brahma is over, the author explains the three types of dissolutions viz. Naimittika (Periodical), Prakrtika (Pertaining to Prakrti) and Atyantika (The Ultimate one, resulting from spiritual knowledge) vide VV. 128-132.

verses.sanskrit: चतुरो वै मनून्पुत्रांश्चातुर्वर्ण्यकराञ्छुभान् । ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा दक्षो धर्मो भवस्तदा
verses.transliteration: caturo vai manūnputrāṃścāturvarṇyakarāñchubhān / brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣo dharmo bhavastadā
verses.translation: At the end of a thousand sets of Caturyugas, •when the period of annihilation of the Yuga arrives, the Prajapati (Lord ofthe Subjects i.e. Brahma) begins to make the subjects abide in him (i.e. reabsorb in him). 1
verses.wordMeaning: At the end of a thousand sets of Caturyugas, •when the period of annihilation of the Yuga arrives, the Prajapati (Lord ofthe Subjects i.e. Brahma) begins to make the subjects abide in him (i.e. reabsorb in him). 1
verses.commentary: Sense: At the end of a thousand sets of Caturyugas, •when the period of annihilation of the Yuga arrives, the Prajapati (Lord ofthe Subjects i.e. Brahma) begins to make the subjects abide in him (i.e. reabsorb in him). 1

verses.sanskrit: तां कन्यां मनसा जग्मुस्त्रयस्ते ब्रह्मणा सह । सत्याभिध्यायिनां तेषां सद्यः कन्या व्यजायत
verses.transliteration: tāṃ kanyāṃ manasā jagmustrayaste brahmaṇā saha / satyābhidhyāyināṃ teṣāṃ sadyaḥ kanyā vyajāyata
verses.translation: Then a continued drought lasting for a hundred years takes place. On account ofit, only those living beings deficient in strength or having very little potentiality on the surface ofthe earth become dissolved and get mingled with the dust.
verses.wordMeaning: Then a continued drought lasting for a hundred years takes place. On account ofit, only those living beings deficient in strength or having very little potentiality on the surface ofthe earth become dissolved and get mingled with the dust.
verses.commentary: Sense: Then a continued drought lasting for a hundred years takes place. On account ofit, only those living beings deficient in strength or having very little potentiality on the surface ofthe earth become dissolved and get mingled with the dust.

verses.sanskrit: सदृशानूपतस्तेषां चतुरो वै कुमारकान् । संसिद्धाः कार्यकरणे संभूतास्ते श्रियान्विताः
verses.transliteration: sadṛśānūpatasteṣāṃ caturo vai kumārakān / saṃsiddhāḥ kāryakaraṇe saṃbhūtāste śriyānvitāḥ
verses.translation: With those rays, the seven suns move up and down. They blaze burning up (everything) like the fire at the close of the Yugas.
verses.wordMeaning: With those rays, the seven suns move up and down. They blaze burning up (everything) like the fire at the close of the Yugas.
verses.commentary: Sense: With those rays, the seven suns move up and down. They blaze burning up (everything) like the fire at the close of the Yugas.

verses.sanskrit: उपभोगासमर्थैश्च सद्योजातैः शरीरकैः । ते दृष्ट्वा तान्स्वयंभूतान्ब्रह्मव्याहारिणस्तदा
verses.transliteration: upabhogāsamarthaiśca sadyojātaiḥ śarīrakaiḥ / te dṛṣṭvā tānsvayaṃbhūtānbrahmavyāhāriṇastadā
verses.translation: Kindled by the waters, those suns with thousands of rays envelop the firmament and stay on, burning the Earth.
verses.wordMeaning: Kindled by the waters, those suns with thousands of rays envelop the firmament and stay on, burning the Earth.
verses.commentary: Sense: Kindled by the waters, those suns with thousands of rays envelop the firmament and stay on, burning the Earth.

verses.sanskrit: सरंब्धा वै व्यकर्षन्त मम पुत्रो ममेत्युत । अभिध्यायात्मनोत्पन्नानूचुर्वै ते परस्परम्
verses.transliteration: saraṃbdhā vai vyakarṣanta mama putro mametyuta / abhidhyāyātmanotpannānūcurvai te parasparam
verses.translation: Being burned by their brilliant flames, the Earth including mountains, rivers and oceans becomes bereft of moisture andj/jscidity.
verses.wordMeaning: Being burned by their brilliant flames, the Earth including mountains, rivers and oceans becomes bereft of moisture andj/jscidity.
verses.commentary: Sense: Being burned by their brilliant flames, the Earth including mountains, rivers and oceans becomes bereft of moisture andj/jscidity.

verses.sanskrit: यो यस्य वपुषा तुल्यो भजतां सततं सुतम् । यस्य यः सदृशश्चापि रूपे वीर्ये च मानतः
verses.transliteration: yo yasya vapuṣā tulyo bhajatāṃ satataṃ sutam / yasya yaḥ sadṛśaścāpi rūpe vīrye ca mānataḥ
verses.translation: Being restrained by those rays ofthe Sun, that burn brightly, that move about in a continuous series and that have variegated colours, the Earth is enveloped entirely, beneath, above and on all sides.
verses.wordMeaning: Being restrained by those rays ofthe Sun, that burn brightly, that move about in a continuous series and that have variegated colours, the Earth is enveloped entirely, beneath, above and on all sides.
verses.commentary: Sense: Being restrained by those rays ofthe Sun, that burn brightly, that move about in a continuous series and that have variegated colours, the Earth is enveloped entirely, beneath, above and on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: तं गृह्णातु स भद्रं वो वर्णतो यस्य यः समः । ध्रुवं रूपं पितुः पुत्रः सो ऽनुरुध्यति सर्वदा
verses.transliteration: taṃ gṛhṇātu sa bhadraṃ vo varṇato yasya yaḥ samaḥ / dhruvaṃ rūpaṃ pituḥ putraḥ so 'nurudhyati sarvadā
verses.translation: VV. 132-178 describe the deluge that pervades the universe after the completion of Brahma's day. The description is common to all Puranas.
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 132-178 describe the deluge that pervades the universe after the completion of Brahma's day. The description is common to all Puranas.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 132-178 describe the deluge that pervades the universe after the completion of Brahma's day. The description is common to all Puranas.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादात्मसमः पुत्रः पितुर्मातुश्च वीर्यतः । एवं ते समयं कृत्वा सर्वेषां जगृहः सुतान्
verses.transliteration: tasmādātmasamaḥ putraḥ piturmātuśca vīryataḥ / evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā sarveṣāṃ jagṛhaḥ sutān
verses.translation: The multifarious fires of the sun become expanded and augmented and then mingle with one another. They then form a single unit— a single flame.
verses.wordMeaning: The multifarious fires of the sun become expanded and augmented and then mingle with one another. They then form a single unit— a single flame.
verses.commentary: Sense: The multifarious fires of the sun become expanded and augmented and then mingle with one another. They then form a single unit— a single flame.

verses.sanskrit: चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे ऽतीते प्राप्ते वैवस्वतस्य ह । रुचेः प्रजापतेः पुत्रो रौच्यो नामाभवत्सुतः
verses.transliteration: cākṣuṣasyāntare 'tīte prāpte vaivasvatasya ha / ruceḥ prajāpateḥ putro raucyo nāmābhavatsutaḥ
verses.translation: It will be the destroyer of all the worlds. That fire takes a circuitous movement and enveloping the set of four worlds burns it up by means ofits fiery splendour.
verses.wordMeaning: It will be the destroyer of all the worlds. That fire takes a circuitous movement and enveloping the set of four worlds burns it up by means ofits fiery splendour.
verses.commentary: Sense: It will be the destroyer of all the worlds. That fire takes a circuitous movement and enveloping the set of four worlds burns it up by means ofits fiery splendour.

verses.sanskrit: भूत्यामुत्पादितो यस्तु भौत्यो नाम कवेः सुतः । वैवस्वतेंऽतरे जातौ द्वौ मनू तु विवस्वतः
verses.transliteration: bhūtyāmutpādito yastu bhautyo nāma kaveḥ sutaḥ / vaivasvateṃ'tare jātau dvau manū tu vivasvataḥ
verses.translation: When everything mobile and immobile becomes dissolved, the Earth devoid of trees and (even) grass may seem like the back of a tortoise.
verses.wordMeaning: When everything mobile and immobile becomes dissolved, the Earth devoid of trees and (even) grass may seem like the back of a tortoise.
verses.commentary: Sense: When everything mobile and immobile becomes dissolved, the Earth devoid of trees and (even) grass may seem like the back of a tortoise.

verses.sanskrit: वैवस्वतो मनुर्यश्च सावर्णो यश्च वै श्रुतः । ज्ञेयः संज्ञासुतो विद्वान्मनुर्वैवस्वतः प्रभुः
verses.transliteration: vaivasvato manuryaśca sāvarṇo yaśca vai śrutaḥ / jñeyaḥ saṃjñāsuto vidvānmanurvaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ
verses.translation: Everything filled with its flames blazes like a solid ball of fire. The entire universe appears like a frying pan.
verses.wordMeaning: Everything filled with its flames blazes like a solid ball of fire. The entire universe appears like a frying pan.
verses.commentary: Sense: Everything filled with its flames blazes like a solid ball of fire. The entire universe appears like a frying pan.

verses.sanskrit: सवर्णायाः सुतश्चान्यः स्मृतो वैवस्वतो मनुः । सावर्णम नवो ये च चत्वारस्तु महर्षिजाः
verses.transliteration: savarṇāyāḥ sutaścānyaḥ smṛto vaivasvato manuḥ / sāvarṇama navo ye ca catvārastu maharṣijāḥ
verses.translation: Whatever be the animals and living beings-on the surface ofthe Earth or within the great oceans become annihi- lated and dissolved and turned into dust (ashes).
verses.wordMeaning: Whatever be the animals and living beings-on the surface ofthe Earth or within the great oceans become annihi- lated and dissolved and turned into dust (ashes).
verses.commentary: Sense: Whatever be the animals and living beings-on the surface ofthe Earth or within the great oceans become annihi- lated and dissolved and turned into dust (ashes).

verses.sanskrit: तपसा संभृतात्मानः स्वेषु मन्वन्तरेषु वै । भविष्येषु भविष्यन्ति सर्वकार्यार्थसाधकाः
verses.transliteration: tapasā saṃbhṛtātmānaḥ sveṣu manvantareṣu vai / bhaviṣyeṣu bhaviṣyanti sarvakāryārthasādhakāḥ
verses.translation: The continents, the mountains, the subcontinents and the great ocean — all these will be reduced to ashes by that universal fire, the soul of everything.
verses.wordMeaning: The continents, the mountains, the subcontinents and the great ocean — all these will be reduced to ashes by that universal fire, the soul of everything.
verses.commentary: Sense: The continents, the mountains, the subcontinents and the great ocean — all these will be reduced to ashes by that universal fire, the soul of everything.

verses.sanskrit: प्रथमे मेरुसावर्णेदक्षपुत्रस्य वै मनोः । परामरीचिगर्भाश्च सुधर्माणश्च ते त्रयः । संभूताश्च महात्मानः सर्वे वैवस्वतेन्तरे
verses.transliteration: prathame merusāvarṇedakṣaputrasya vai manoḥ / parāmarīcigarbhāśca sudharmāṇaśca te trayaḥ / saṃbhūtāśca mahātmānaḥ sarve vaivasvatentare
verses.translation: The kindled fire resorting to the earth blazes and drinks up water from the seas, rivers, nether worlds completely from all sides.
verses.wordMeaning: The kindled fire resorting to the earth blazes and drinks up water from the seas, rivers, nether worlds completely from all sides.
verses.commentary: Sense: The kindled fire resorting to the earth blazes and drinks up water from the seas, rivers, nether worlds completely from all sides.

verses.sanskrit: दक्षपुत्रस्य पुत्रास्ते रोहितस्य प्रजापतेः । भविष्यन्ति भविष्यास्तु एकैको द्वादशो गणः
verses.transliteration: dakṣaputrasya putrāste rohitasya prajāpateḥ / bhaviṣyanti bhaviṣyāstu ekaiko dvādaśo gaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Increased in its dimensions, this enkindled Sarhvar- taka fire, of terrible form transcends the mountains and planets and annihilates the worlds.
verses.wordMeaning: Increased in its dimensions, this enkindled Sarhvar- taka fire, of terrible form transcends the mountains and planets and annihilates the worlds.
verses.commentary: Sense: Increased in its dimensions, this enkindled Sarhvar- taka fire, of terrible form transcends the mountains and planets and annihilates the worlds.

verses.sanskrit: ऐश्वरश्च ग्रहो राहुर्वाकुर्वंशस्तथैव च । पारा द्वादश विज्ञेया उत्तरांस्तु निबोधत
verses.transliteration: aiśvaraśca graho rāhurvākurvaṃśastathaiva ca / pārā dvādaśa vijñeyā uttarāṃstu nibodhata
verses.translation: Thereafter, it breaks through the Earth and dries up Rasatala. After burning up Patala completely, it burns up the world ofwind in the end.
verses.wordMeaning: Thereafter, it breaks through the Earth and dries up Rasatala. After burning up Patala completely, it burns up the world ofwind in the end.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thereafter, it breaks through the Earth and dries up Rasatala. After burning up Patala completely, it burns up the world ofwind in the end.

verses.sanskrit: वाजिपो वाजिजिच्चैव प्रभूतिश्च ककुद्यथ । दधिक्रावा विपक्वश्च प्रणीतो विजयो मधुः
verses.transliteration: vājipo vājijiccaiva prabhūtiśca kakudyatha / dadhikrāvā vipakvaśca praṇīto vijayo madhuḥ
verses.translation: Some of them are dark in colour like the blue lotus, some resemble the water lilies. Some appear like Vaidurya (Lapis Lazuli). Others resemble Indranlla (blue Sapphire).
verses.wordMeaning: Some of them are dark in colour like the blue lotus, some resemble the water lilies. Some appear like Vaidurya (Lapis Lazuli). Others resemble Indranlla (blue Sapphire).
verses.commentary: Sense: Some of them are dark in colour like the blue lotus, some resemble the water lilies. Some appear like Vaidurya (Lapis Lazuli). Others resemble Indranlla (blue Sapphire).

verses.sanskrit: उतथ्योत्तमकौ द्वौ तु द्वादशैते मरीचयः । सुधर्माणस्तु वक्ष्यामि नामतस्तान्निबोधत
verses.transliteration: utathyottamakau dvau tu dvādaśaite marīcayaḥ / sudharmāṇastu vakṣyāmi nāmatastānnibodhata
verses.translation: Other clouds appear white like conch and jasmine flowers as well as dark like the black pigment. Some clouds are smoke-coloured and some are yellow.
verses.wordMeaning: Other clouds appear white like conch and jasmine flowers as well as dark like the black pigment. Some clouds are smoke-coloured and some are yellow.
verses.commentary: Sense: Other clouds appear white like conch and jasmine flowers as well as dark like the black pigment. Some clouds are smoke-coloured and some are yellow.

verses.sanskrit: वर्णस्तथाथगर्विश्च भुरण्यो व्रजनो ऽमितः । अमितो द्रवकेतुश्च जंभो ऽथाजस्तु शक्रकः
verses.transliteration: varṇastathāthagarviśca bhuraṇyo vrajano 'mitaḥ / amito dravaketuśca jaṃbho 'thājastu śakrakaḥ
verses.translation: Some clouds have a shining lustre like the colour of a donkey. Similarly, some resemble the colour of the lac exuda- tion. Others appear like the Manalisila (Red Arsenic) and other clouds have the colour of doves.
verses.wordMeaning: Some clouds have a shining lustre like the colour of a donkey. Similarly, some resemble the colour of the lac exuda- tion. Others appear like the Manalisila (Red Arsenic) and other clouds have the colour of doves.
verses.commentary: Sense: Some clouds have a shining lustre like the colour of a donkey. Similarly, some resemble the colour of the lac exuda- tion. Others appear like the Manalisila (Red Arsenic) and other clouds have the colour of doves.

verses.sanskrit: सुनेमिर्द्युतयश्चैव सुधर्माणः प्रकीर्तिताः । तेषामिन्द्रस्तदा भाव्यो ह्यद्भुतो नाम नामतः
verses.transliteration: sunemirdyutayaścaiva sudharmāṇaḥ prakīrtitāḥ / teṣāmindrastadā bhāvyo hyadbhuto nāma nāmataḥ
verses.translation: Some clouds resemble the glow-worm. Some are
verses.wordMeaning: Some clouds resemble the glow-worm. Some are
verses.commentary: Sense: Some clouds resemble the glow-worm. Some are

verses.sanskrit: स्कन्दो ऽसौ पार्वतीयो वै कार्तिकेयस्तु पावकिः । मेधातिथिश्च पौलस्त्यो वसुः काश्यप एवं च
verses.transliteration: skando 'sau pārvatīyo vai kārtikeyastu pāvakiḥ / medhātithiśca paulastyo vasuḥ kāśyapa evaṃ ca
verses.translation: Some of the clouds are ofthe size of an excellent city. Some can be compared to herds ofelephants. Some clouds shine like huge mountains. Some clouds appearlike an extensive flat ground.
verses.wordMeaning: Some of the clouds are ofthe size of an excellent city. Some can be compared to herds ofelephants. Some clouds shine like huge mountains. Some clouds appearlike an extensive flat ground.
verses.commentary: Sense: Some of the clouds are ofthe size of an excellent city. Some can be compared to herds ofelephants. Some clouds shine like huge mountains. Some clouds appearlike an extensive flat ground.

verses.sanskrit: ज्योतिष्मान्भार्गवाश्चैव द्युतिमानङ्गिरास्तथा । वसिनश्चैव वासिष्ठ आत्रेयो हव्यवाहनः
verses.transliteration: jyotiṣmānbhārgavāścaiva dyutimānaṅgirāstathā / vasinaścaiva vāsiṣṭha ātreyo havyavāhanaḥ
verses.translation: Some clouds resemble the hall ofgames. Some can be compared to shoals offish. The clouds have different forms. They are aweful in appearance and make terrific thundering sound.
verses.wordMeaning: Some clouds resemble the hall ofgames. Some can be compared to shoals offish. The clouds have different forms. They are aweful in appearance and make terrific thundering sound.
verses.commentary: Sense: Some clouds resemble the hall ofgames. Some can be compared to shoals offish. The clouds have different forms. They are aweful in appearance and make terrific thundering sound.

verses.sanskrit: सुतपाः पौलहश्चैव सप्तैते रोहितेतरे । धृतिकेतुर्दीप्तिकेतुः शापहस्तनिरामयाः
verses.transliteration: sutapāḥ paulahaścaiva saptaite rohitetare / dhṛtiketurdīptiketuḥ śāpahastanirāmayāḥ
verses.translation: Then the clouds fill the entire area of the firmament. After that, these clouds, producing terrific rumbling sound group themselves in seven, identifying themselves with the- Suns, and they extinguish the fire. Then those clouds shower rain in huge torrents. They destroy'the whole of extremely terrific and inauspicious fire. With the waters so profusely showered, the universe becomes filled up with it. With its splendour attacked and subdued by the waters, the fire enters into the waters.
verses.wordMeaning: Then the clouds fill the entire area of the firmament. After that, these clouds, producing terrific rumbling sound group themselves in seven, identifying themselves with the- Suns, and they extinguish the fire. Then those clouds shower rain in huge torrents.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Then the clouds fill the entire area of the firmament. After that, these clouds, producing terrific rumbling sound group themselves in seven, identifying themselves with the- Suns, and they extinguish the fire. Then those clouds shower rain in huge torrents.…

verses.sanskrit: पृथुश्रवास्तथानीको भूरिद्युम्नो बृहद्यशः । प्रथमस्य तु सावर्णेर्नव पुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः
verses.transliteration: pṛthuśravāstathānīko bhūridyumno bṛhadyaśaḥ / prathamasya tu sāvarṇernava putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
verses.translation: He has the brilliant complexion of the Sun. He is the protector of the Universe. He is unparalleled, the only one (without a second), the first, quickly overpowerer (of the mighty), a cosmogonic power (lit. born of a golden egg), the Supreme Person, the great one. It is recited (in the scriptures) that he is beyond the quality called Rajas.
verses.wordMeaning: He has the brilliant complexion of the Sun. He is the protector of the Universe. He is unparalleled, the only one (without a second), the first, quickly overpowerer (of the mighty), a cosmogonic power (lit. born of a golden egg), the Supreme Person, the great one.…
verses.commentary: Sense: He has the brilliant complexion of the Sun. He is the protector of the Universe. He is unparalleled, the only one (without a second), the first, quickly overpowerer (of the mighty), a cosmogonic power (lit. born of a golden egg), the Supreme Person, the great one.…

verses.sanskrit: दशमे त्वथ पर्याये धर्मपुत्रस्य वै मनोः । द्वीतीयस्य तु सावर्णेर्भाव्यस्यैवान्तरे मनोः
verses.transliteration: daśame tvatha paryāye dharmaputrasya vai manoḥ / dvītīyasya tu sāvarṇerbhāvyasyaivāntare manoḥ
verses.translation: At the end of the thousand sets of four Yugas, when all space is flooded with water on all sides, the lord be- comes desirous of sleep. As he does not wish for light, he creates the Night.
verses.wordMeaning: At the end of the thousand sets of four Yugas, when all space is flooded with water on all sides, the lord be- comes desirous of sleep. As he does not wish for light, he creates the Night.
verses.commentary: Sense: At the end of the thousand sets of four Yugas, when all space is flooded with water on all sides, the lord be- comes desirous of sleep. As he does not wish for light, he creates the Night.

verses.sanskrit: सुधामानो विरुद्धाश्च द्वावेव तु गणौ स्मृतौ । दीप्तिमन्तश्च ते सर्वे शतसंख्याश्च ते समाः
verses.transliteration: sudhāmāno viruddhāśca dvāveva tu gaṇau smṛtau / dīptimantaśca te sarve śatasaṃkhyāśca te samāḥ
verses.translation: When the Night comes to a close, Prajapati wakes up. He becomes induced with a desire to create. He then once again applies his mind to the activity of creation.
verses.wordMeaning: When the Night comes to a close, Prajapati wakes up. He becomes induced with a desire to create. He then once again applies his mind to the activity of creation.
verses.commentary: Sense: When the Night comes to a close, Prajapati wakes up. He becomes induced with a desire to create. He then once again applies his mind to the activity of creation.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणानां यच्छतं प्रोक्तं ऋषिभिः पुरषेति वै । देवास्ते वै भविष्यन्ति धर्मपुत्रस्य वै मनोः
verses.transliteration: prāṇānāṃ yacchataṃ proktaṃ ṛṣibhiḥ puraṣeti vai / devāste vai bhaviṣyanti dharmaputrasya vai manoḥ
verses.translation: When the night becomes dawn, all those living beings are born again from Brahma of unmanifest source of origin.
verses.wordMeaning: When the night becomes dawn, all those living beings are born again from Brahma of unmanifest source of origin.
verses.commentary: Sense: When the night becomes dawn, all those living beings are born again from Brahma of unmanifest source of origin.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामिन्द्रस्तथा विद्वान्भविष्यः शान्तिरुच्यते । हविष्मान्पौलहः श्रीमान्सुकीर्तिश्चाथ भार्गवः
verses.transliteration: teṣāmindrastathā vidvānbhaviṣyaḥ śāntirucyate / haviṣmānpaulahaḥ śrīmānsukīrtiścātha bhārgavaḥ
verses.translation: The Sages, the Manus and the four types of living beings— all these are born again. It is mentioned that even, those Siddhas do have birth and death.
verses.wordMeaning: The Sages, the Manus and the four types of living beings— all these are born again. It is mentioned that even, those Siddhas do have birth and death.
verses.commentary: Sense: The Sages, the Manus and the four types of living beings— all these are born again. It is mentioned that even, those Siddhas do have birth and death.

verses.sanskrit: आपोमूर्तिस्तथात्रेयो वसिष्ठश्चापवः स्मृतः । पौलस्त्यो ऽप्रतिमश्चापि नाभागश्चैव काश्यपः
verses.transliteration: āpomūrtistathātreyo vasiṣṭhaścāpavaḥ smṛtaḥ / paulastyo 'pratimaścāpi nābhāgaścaiva kāśyapaḥ
verses.translation: Just as the rising and setting of the Sun in this world happens regularly, so also (it should) be remembered that the birth and death of all living beings are happening; regularly.
verses.wordMeaning: Just as the rising and setting of the Sun in this world happens regularly, so also (it should) be remembered that the birth and death of all living beings are happening; regularly.
verses.commentary: Sense: Just as the rising and setting of the Sun in this world happens regularly, so also (it should) be remembered that the birth and death of all living beings are happening; regularly.

verses.sanskrit: अभिमन्युश्चाङ्गिरसः सप्तैते परमर्षयः । सुक्षेत्रश्चोत्तमौजाश्च भूरिसेनश्च वीर्यवान्
verses.transliteration: abhimanyuścāṅgirasaḥ saptaite paramarṣayaḥ / sukṣetraścottamaujāśca bhūrisenaśca vīryavān
verses.translation: When two thousand Caturyugas are completed
verses.wordMeaning: When two thousand Caturyugas are completed
verses.commentary: Sense: When two thousand Caturyugas are completed

verses.sanskrit: शतानीको निरामित्रो वृषसेनो जयद्रथः । भूरिद्युम्नः सुवर्चाश्च दशैतेमानवाः स्मृताः
verses.transliteration: śatānīko nirāmitro vṛṣaseno jayadrathaḥ / bhūridyumnaḥ suvarcāśca daśaitemānavāḥ smṛtāḥ
verses.translation: A matra has been made equal to a Nimesa (winking of the eye) by a person at leisure. Fifteen winkings of human eyes make one Kaffha.'
verses.wordMeaning: A matra has been made equal to a Nimesa (winking of the eye) by a person at leisure. Fifteen winkings of human eyes make one Kaffha.'
verses.commentary: Sense: A matra has been made equal to a Nimesa (winking of the eye) by a person at leisure. Fifteen winkings of human eyes make one Kaffha.'

verses.sanskrit: एकादशे तु पर्याये सावर्णे वै तृतीयके । निर्वाणरतयो देवाः कामगा वै मनोजवाः
verses.transliteration: ekādaśe tu paryāye sāvarṇe vai tṛtīyake / nirvāṇaratayo devāḥ kāmagā vai manojavāḥ
verses.translation: (Defective Text) (?) Nine winkings make a Ksana or five winkings make one Ksana, Twenty winkings make one Kastha. Three Kdsflias make one Prastha (?). Seven Prasthas make one udaka (?). One more (i.e. Eight Prasthas) make one Lava, * (?)
verses.wordMeaning: (Defective Text) (?) Nine winkings make a Ksana or five winkings make one Ksana, Twenty winkings make one Kastha. Three Kdsflias make one Prastha (?). Seven Prasthas make one udaka (?). One more (i.e. Eight Prasthas) make one Lava, * (?)
verses.commentary: Sense: (Defective Text) (?) Nine winkings make a Ksana or five winkings make one Ksana, Twenty winkings make one Kastha. Three Kdsflias make one Prastha (?). Seven Prasthas make one udaka (?). One more (i.e. Eight Prasthas) make one Lava, * (?)

verses.sanskrit: गणास्त्वेते त्रयः ख्याता देवातानां महात्मनाम् । एकैकस्त्रिंशतस्तेषां गणस्तु त्रिदिवौकसाम्
verses.transliteration: gaṇāstvete trayaḥ khyātā devātānāṃ mahātmanām / ekaikastriṃśatasteṣāṃ gaṇastu tridivaukasām
verses.translation: It should be known that thirty Lavas make one Kali, Thirty Ka/ds make one Muhurta, Thirty Muhurtas make one day and night. This is the position.
verses.wordMeaning: It should be known that thirty Lavas make one Kali, Thirty Ka/ds make one Muhurta, Thirty Muhurtas make one day and night. This is the position.
verses.commentary: Sense: It should be known that thirty Lavas make one Kali, Thirty Ka/ds make one Muhurta, Thirty Muhurtas make one day and night. This is the position.

verses.sanskrit: मासस्याहानि त्रिंशत्तु यानि वै कवयो विदुः । निर्वाणरतयो देवा रात्रयस्तु विहङ्गमाः
verses.transliteration: māsasyāhāni triṃśattu yāni vai kavayo viduḥ / nirvāṇaratayo devā rātrayastu vihaṅgamāḥ
verses.translation: One day and night consists of more than six hundred Ka/as (30 x 30 = 900). These should be known in accordance with the movements of the moon and the Sun.
verses.wordMeaning: One day and night consists of more than six hundred Ka/as (30 x 30 = 900). These should be known in accordance with the movements of the moon and the Sun.
verses.commentary: Sense: One day and night consists of more than six hundred Ka/as (30 x 30 = 900). These should be known in accordance with the movements of the moon and the Sun.

verses.sanskrit: गणस्तृतीयो यः प्रोक्ते देवतानां भविष्यति । मनोजवा मूरूर्त्तास्तु इति देवाः प्रकीर्तिताः
verses.transliteration: gaṇastṛtīyo yaḥ prokte devatānāṃ bhaviṣyati / manojavā mūrūrttāstu iti devāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
verses.translation: The units Abhuta -samp lava.
verses.wordMeaning: The units Abhuta -samp lava.
verses.commentary: Sense: The units Abhuta -samp lava.

verses.sanskrit: एते हि ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा भविष्या मानवाः स्मृताः । तेषामिद्रो वृषा नाम भविष्यः सुरराट् ततः
verses.transliteration: ete hi brahmaṇaḥ putrā bhaviṣyā mānavāḥ smṛtāḥ / teṣāmidro vṛṣā nāma bhaviṣyaḥ surarāṭ tataḥ
verses.translation: In the same manner thirteen Palas of water con- stitute a Jalaprastha according to Magadha reckoning.
verses.wordMeaning: In the same manner thirteen Palas of water con- stitute a Jalaprastha according to Magadha reckoning.
verses.commentary: Sense: In the same manner thirteen Palas of water con- stitute a Jalaprastha according to Magadha reckoning.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां सप्तऋषींश्चापि कीर्त्यमानान्निवौधत । हविष्मान्काश्यपश्चापि वपुष्मांश्चैव भार्गवः
verses.transliteration: teṣāṃ saptaṛṣīṃścāpi kīrtyamānānnivaudhata / haviṣmānkāśyapaścāpi vapuṣmāṃścaiva bhārgavaḥ
verses.translation: On learning this the sages (become) surprised. They considered it wonderful. Then they sought the knowledge regarding the division of the number of days.
verses.wordMeaning: On learning this the sages (become) surprised. They considered it wonderful. Then they sought the knowledge regarding the division of the number of days.
verses.commentary: Sense: On learning this the sages (become) surprised. They considered it wonderful. Then they sought the knowledge regarding the division of the number of days.

verses.sanskrit: आरुणिश्च तथात्रेयो वसिष्ठो नग एव च । पुष्टिराङ्गिरसो ज्ञेयः पौलस्त्यो निश्चरस्तथा
verses.transliteration: āruṇiśca tathātreyo vasiṣṭho naga eva ca / puṣṭirāṅgiraso jñeyaḥ paulastyo niścarastathā
verses.translation: We wish to hear the measurement and calculation according to human reckoning. Let it be brief with very few letters and words. Human calculation alone is in accordance with our opinion.
verses.wordMeaning: We wish to hear the measurement and calculation according to human reckoning. Let it be brief with very few letters and words. Human calculation alone is in accordance with our opinion.
verses.commentary: Sense: We wish to hear the measurement and calculation according to human reckoning. Let it be brief with very few letters and words. Human calculation alone is in accordance with our opinion.

verses.sanskrit: पौलहो ह्यतितेजश्च देवा ह्येकादशेन्तरे । सर्ववेगः सुधर्मा च देवानीकः पुरोवहः
verses.transliteration: paulaho hyatitejaśca devā hyekādaśentare / sarvavegaḥ sudharmā ca devānīkaḥ purovahaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing their requests, the wind-god engaged in what is beneficial to the worlds, said succinctly as follows
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing their requests, the wind-god engaged in what is beneficial to the worlds, said succinctly as follows
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing their requests, the wind-god engaged in what is beneficial to the worlds, said succinctly as follows

verses.sanskrit: द्वादशे त्वथ पर्याये रुद्रपुत्रस्य वै मनोः । चतुर्थो रुद्रसावर्णो देवांस्तस्यान्तरे शृणु
verses.transliteration: dvādaśe tvatha paryāye rudraputrasya vai manoḥ / caturtho rudrasāvarṇo devāṃstasyāntare śṛṇu
verses.translation: When the world is flooded with water, when, everything mobile is dissolved and destroyed, when the activity of annihilation is concluded, when Prajapati becomes quiescent, when there is no light, when everything is burnt down and enveloped in the nocturnal darkness and when it is presided over by Tsvara— that is the time when a vast expanse of Sea comes into being. The extent of duration of the vast expanse of Sea is as much as that of the day ofthe lord. The night is the period when there exists the Salila (motionless water). The period when it recedes is remembered as the daytime.
verses.wordMeaning: When the world is flooded with water, when, everything mobile is dissolved and destroyed, when the activity of annihilation is concluded, when Prajapati becomes quiescent, when there is no light,…

verses.commentary: Sense: The burning wick of the lamp becomes extinguished by a violent gust of wind. In the same manner Brahma becomes quiescent due to Pratisarga.

verses.sanskrit: इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते उत्तरभागे चतुर्थ उपसंहारपादे आभूतसंप्लवाख्यवर्णनं नाम प्रथमो ऽध्यायः वायुरुवाच असाधारणवृत्तैस्तु हुतशेषादिभिर्जनैः । धर्मा वैशेषिकाश्चैव आचीर्णाः सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः
verses.transliteration: iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte uttarabhāge caturtha upasaṃhārapāde ābhūtasaṃplavākhyavarṇanaṃ nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ vāyuruvāca asādhāraṇavṛttaistu hutaśeṣādibhirjanaiḥ / dharmā vaiśeṣikāścaiva ācīrṇāḥ sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ
verses.translation: Special holy rites have been duly performed by persons ofacute discernment and of extraordinary habits and practices, with the residue ofwhat is consigned to the sacred fire in the form of Homa and also with other things.
verses.wordMeaning: Special holy rites have been duly performed by persons ofacute discernment and of extraordinary habits and practices, with the residue ofwhat is consigned to the sacred fire in the form of Homa and also with other things.
verses.commentary: Sense: Special holy rites have been duly performed by persons ofacute discernment and of extraordinary habits and practices, with the residue ofwhat is consigned to the sacred fire in the form of Homa and also with other things.

verses.sanskrit: ते देवैः सह तिष्ठन्ति महर्लोकनिवासिनः । चतुर्दशैते मनवः कीर्तिताः कीर्तिवर्द्धनाः
verses.transliteration: te devaiḥ saha tiṣṭhanti maharlokanivāsinaḥ / caturdaśaite manavaḥ kīrtitāḥ kīrtivarddhanāḥ
verses.translation: VV. 239-243 describe what happens when the life of god Brahma terminates.
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 239-243 describe what happens when the life of god Brahma terminates.
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 239-243 describe what happens when the life of god Brahma terminates.

verses.sanskrit: अतीता वर्त्तमानाश्च तथैवानागताश्च ये । देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव मनवः पितरस्तथा
verses.transliteration: atītā varttamānāśca tathaivānāgatāśca ye / devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva manavaḥ pitarastathā
verses.translation: Although the title ofthe chapter leads to believe that it must be a description only of Siva-loka (the region of Siva), it is a description of Bhuvana-koia or different regions (lokas) constituting the universe. Siva's region comrs at the end.
verses.wordMeaning: Although the title ofthe chapter leads to believe that it must be a description only of Siva-loka (the region of Siva), it is a description of Bhuvana-koia or different regions (lokas) constituting the universe. Siva's region comrs at the end.
verses.commentary: Sense: Although the title ofthe chapter leads to believe that it must be a description only of Siva-loka (the region of Siva), it is a description of Bhuvana-koia or different regions (lokas) constituting the universe. Siva's region comrs at the end.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे ह्युक्ता मयातीत महर्लोकं समाश्रिताः । ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैर्धार्मिकैः सहितैः सरैः
verses.transliteration: sarve hyuktā mayātīta maharlokaṃ samāśritāḥ / brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyairdhārmikaiḥ sahitaiḥ saraiḥ
verses.translation: "Only fourteen Sth&nas (abodes) have been created by the great sages. They are those that are called Lokas 1 (Worlds) where men stay.
verses.wordMeaning: "Only fourteen Sth&nas (abodes) have been created by the great sages. They are those that are called Lokas 1 (Worlds) where men stay.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Only fourteen Sth&nas (abodes) have been created by the great sages. They are those that are called Lokas 1 (Worlds) where men stay.

verses.sanskrit: तैस्तथाकारिभिर्युक्तैः श्रद्धावद्भिरदर्पितैः । वर्णाश्रमाणान्धर्मेषु श्रौतस्मार्त्तेषु संस्थितैः । विनिवृत्ताधिकारास्ते यावन्मन्वन्तरक्षयः
verses.transliteration: taistathākāribhiryuktaiḥ śraddhāvadbhiradarpitaiḥ / varṇāśramāṇāndharmeṣu śrautasmārtteṣu saṃsthitaiḥ / vinivṛttādhikārāste yāvanmanvantarakṣayaḥ
verses.translation: They say that Seven of them are Krtas and Seven are Akrtas. The seven worlds beginning with Bhuh and ending with Satya are the Krtas.
verses.wordMeaning: They say that Seven of them are Krtas and Seven are Akrtas. The seven worlds beginning with Bhuh and ending with Satya are the Krtas.
verses.commentary: Sense: They say that Seven of them are Krtas and Seven are Akrtas. The seven worlds beginning with Bhuh and ending with Satya are the Krtas.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषय ऊचुः महर्ल्लोकेति यत्प्रोक्तं मातरिश्वंस्त्वया विभोः
verses.transliteration: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ maharlloketi yatproktaṃ mātariśvaṃstvayā vibhoḥ
verses.translation: The Akrtas are only seven. They are the abodes that are Prakrtas (evolved by Prakrti). These Sth&nas have been
verses.wordMeaning: The Akrtas are only seven. They are the abodes that are Prakrtas (evolved by Prakrti). These Sth&nas have been
verses.commentary: Sense: The Akrtas are only seven. They are the abodes that are Prakrtas (evolved by Prakrti). These Sth&nas have been

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिलोके तु कर्त्तव्यं तत्रकिं समधिष्ठितम् । प्रोवाच मधुरं वाक्यं यथा तत्त्वेन तत्त्ववित्
verses.transliteration: pratiloke tu karttavyaṃ tatrakiṃ samadhiṣṭhitam / provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ yathā tattvena tattvavit
verses.translation: VV. 8-40 describe the seven worlds viz 1. Bhur, 2. Bliuvas, 3. Svar,
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 8-40 describe the seven worlds viz 1. Bhur, 2. Bliuvas, 3. Svar,
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 8-40 describe the seven worlds viz 1. Bhur, 2. Bliuvas, 3. Svar,

verses.sanskrit: वायुरुवाच चतर्दशैव स्थानानि निर्मितानि महर्षिभिः । लोकाख्यानि तु यानि स्युर्येषां तिष्ठन्ति मानवाः
verses.transliteration: vāyuruvāca catardaśaiva sthānāni nirmitāni maharṣibhiḥ / lokākhyāni tu yāni syuryeṣāṃ tiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ
verses.translation: Maliar (in details) 5. Jana, 6. Tapas and 7. Satya. These seven are called krtas. The location of 1-4 is (1) The earth, (2) The space between the earth and the sun, (3) The space between the sun and Dhruva (The Polar Star) •(4) the space between Dhruva and Jana-loka is Mahar-loka (V V. 39-40). VV. 22-25 explain the terms jfana-loka (causing birth of people like Manu), Tapas (Region for performers of Penance) and Satya ( = SaUamatra, - of pure existence, the region of Brahma).
verses.wordMeaning: Maliar (in details) 5. Jana, 6. Tapas and 7. Satya. These seven are called krtas. The location of 1-4 is (1) The earth, (2) The space between the earth and the sun,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Maliar (in details) 5. Jana, 6. Tapas and 7. Satya. These seven are called krtas. The location of 1-4 is (1) The earth, (2) The space between the earth and the sun,…

verses.sanskrit: सप्त तेषु कृतान्याहुरकृतानि तु सप्त वै । भूरादयस्तु सत्यान्ताः सप्त लोकाः कृतास्त्विह
verses.transliteration: sapta teṣu kṛtānyāhurakṛtāni tu sapta vai / bhūrādayastu satyāntāḥ sapta lokāḥ kṛtāstviha
verses.translation: Jana, Tapa and Satya — These three worlds are Ekintikas (exclusive ones). They remain steady till the Prasam - yama (Ultimate Re-absorption).
verses.wordMeaning: Jana, Tapa and Satya — These three worlds are Ekintikas (exclusive ones). They remain steady till the Prasam - yama (Ultimate Re-absorption).
verses.commentary: Sense: Jana, Tapa and Satya — These three worlds are Ekintikas (exclusive ones). They remain steady till the Prasam - yama (Ultimate Re-absorption).

verses.sanskrit: अकृतानि तु सप्तैव प्राकृतानि तु यानि वै । स्थानानि स्थानिभिः सार्द्धं कृतानि तु निबन्धनम्
verses.transliteration: akṛtāni tu saptaiva prākṛtāni tu yāni vai / sthānāni sthānibhiḥ sārddhaṃ kṛtāni tu nibandhanam
verses.translation: Due to the utterance of Mahar the Maharloka came into existence. The abode of the Devas whose tenure of office has come to an end is there.
verses.wordMeaning: Due to the utterance of Mahar the Maharloka came into existence. The abode of the Devas whose tenure of office has come to an end is there.
verses.commentary: Sense: Due to the utterance of Mahar the Maharloka came into existence. The abode of the Devas whose tenure of office has come to an end is there.

verses.sanskrit: पृथिवी चान्तरीक्षं च दिव्यं यच्च महः स्मृतम् । स्थानान्येतानि चत्वारि स्मृतान्यावर्णकानि च
verses.transliteration: pṛthivī cāntarīkṣaṃ ca divyaṃ yacca mahaḥ smṛtam / sthānānyetāni catvāri smṛtānyāvarṇakāni ca
verses.translation: The sages Arigirases resort to the Bhuvarloka. Those persons i.e. the Devas who reside in the constellations and planets are (called) Vaimdnikas.
verses.wordMeaning: The sages Arigirases resort to the Bhuvarloka. Those persons i.e. the Devas who reside in the constellations and planets are (called) Vaimdnikas.
verses.commentary: Sense: The sages Arigirases resort to the Bhuvarloka. Those persons i.e. the Devas who reside in the constellations and planets are (called) Vaimdnikas.

verses.sanskrit: क्षयातिशययुक्तानि तथायुक्तानि चक्षते । यानि नैमित्तिकानि स्युस्तिष्ठन्त्याभूतसंप्लवात्
verses.transliteration: kṣayātiśayayuktāni tathāyuktāni cakṣate / yāni naimittikāni syustiṣṭhantyābhūtasaṃplavāt
verses.translation: The worlds having Bhurloka as the first and Mahar as the last, are proclaimed thus. Those seven Suryas (at the time of ultimate dissolution) burn all those worlds by means of their flames.
verses.wordMeaning: The worlds having Bhurloka as the first and Mahar as the last, are proclaimed thus. Those seven Suryas (at the time of ultimate dissolution) burn all those worlds by means of their flames.
verses.commentary: Sense: The worlds having Bhurloka as the first and Mahar as the last, are proclaimed thus. Those seven Suryas (at the time of ultimate dissolution) burn all those worlds by means of their flames.

verses.sanskrit: जनस्तपश्च सत्यं च स्थानान्येतानि त्रीणि तु । एकान्तिकानि तानि स्युस्तिष्ठन्तीहाप्रसंयमात्
verses.transliteration: janastapaśca satyaṃ ca sthānānyetāni trīṇi tu / ekāntikāni tāni syustiṣṭhantīhāprasaṃyamāt
verses.translation: (Defective Text) The sixth world viz. Tapas is the world remembered as the place causing return of all the fourteen Manus in the course of Manvantaras including those of Savarnas.
verses.wordMeaning: (Defective Text) The sixth world viz. Tapas is the world remembered as the place causing return of all the fourteen Manus in the course of Manvantaras including those of Savarnas.
verses.commentary: Sense: (Defective Text) The sixth world viz. Tapas is the world remembered as the place causing return of all the fourteen Manus in the course of Manvantaras including those of Savarnas.

verses.sanskrit: व्यक्तानि तु प्रवक्ष्यामि स्थानान्येतानि सप्त वै । भूर्लोकः प्रथमस्तेषां द्वितीयस्तु भुवः स्मृतः
verses.transliteration: vyaktāni tu pravakṣyāmi sthānānyetāni sapta vai / bhūrlokaḥ prathamasteṣāṃ dvitīyastu bhuvaḥ smṛtaḥ
verses.translation: The space between Dhruva and the Jana Loka is called Maharloka.
verses.wordMeaning: The space between Dhruva and the Jana Loka is called Maharloka.
verses.commentary: Sense: The space between Dhruva and the Jana Loka is called Maharloka.

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्तृतीयस्तु विज्ञेयश्चतुर्थो वै महः स्मृतः । जनस्तु पञ्चमो लोकस्तपः षष्ठो विभाव्यते
verses.transliteration: svastṛtīyastu vijñeyaścaturtho vai mahaḥ smṛtaḥ / janastu pañcamo lokastapaḥ ṣaṣṭho vibhāvyate
verses.translation: Their mental achievement should be known as very pure on account of mutual interaction.
verses.wordMeaning: Their mental achievement should be known as very pure on account of mutual interaction.
verses.commentary: Sense: Their mental achievement should be known as very pure on account of mutual interaction.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यस्तु सप्तमो लोको निरालोकस्ततः परम् । भूरिति व्याहृतेः पूर्व भूर्लोकश्च ततो ऽभवत्
verses.transliteration: satyastu saptamo loko nirālokastataḥ param / bhūriti vyāhṛteḥ pūrva bhūrlokaśca tato 'bhavat
verses.translation: All those groups (ofDevas) Yama and others who reside in Mahar loka resort to Janaloka itself when the Maharloka is ablaze and "burnt up.
verses.wordMeaning: All those groups (ofDevas) Yama and others who reside in Mahar loka resort to Janaloka itself when the Maharloka is ablaze and "burnt up.
verses.commentary: Sense: All those groups (ofDevas) Yama and others who reside in Mahar loka resort to Janaloka itself when the Maharloka is ablaze and "burnt up.

verses.sanskrit: द्वीतीयो भुव इत्युक्त अन्तरिक्षं ततो ऽभवत् । तृतीयं स्वरितीत्युक्तो दिवं प्रादुर्बभूव ह
verses.transliteration: dvītīyo bhuva ityukta antarikṣaṃ tato 'bhavat / tṛtīyaṃ svaritītyukto divaṃ prādurbabhūva ha
verses.translation: All those who are the inhabitants of that place are persons with subtle bodies. These (Yama and others) acquire the same ability or equal potentiality as the inhabitants (of Janaloka) and they are equipped with a physical form similar to that of those persons.
verses.wordMeaning: All those who are the inhabitants of that place are persons with subtle bodies. These (Yama and others) acquire the same ability or equal potentiality as the inhabitants (of Janaloka) and they are equipped with a physical form similar to that of those persons.
verses.commentary: Sense: All those who are the inhabitants of that place are persons with subtle bodies. These (Yama and others) acquire the same ability or equal potentiality as the inhabitants (of Janaloka) and they are equipped with a physical form similar to that of those persons.

verses.sanskrit: व्याहारैस्त्रिभिरेतैस्तु ब्रह्मा लोकमकल्पयत् । ततो भूः पार्थिवो लोको ह्यन्तरिक्षं भूवः स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: vyāhāraistribhiretaistu brahmā lokamakalpayat / tato bhūḥ pārthivo loko hyantarikṣaṃ bhūvaḥ smṛtam
verses.translation: In VV. 47-68, Vayu describes how gods etc. resort to Janaloka when Maharloka suffers from the samvartaka fire at the end of the world. He states how the time is endless; and how in the same process ofthe same gods, sages etc? taking re-incarnation time continues (ad infinitum).
verses.wordMeaning: In VV. 47-68, Vayu describes how gods etc. resort to Janaloka when Maharloka suffers from the samvartaka fire at the end of the world. He states how the time is endless; and how in the same process ofthe same gods, sages etc? taking re-incarnation time continues (ad infinitum).
verses.commentary: Sense: In VV. 47-68, Vayu describes how gods etc. resort to Janaloka when Maharloka suffers from the samvartaka fire at the end of the world. He states how the time is endless; and how in the same process ofthe same gods, sages etc? taking re-incarnation time continues (ad infinitum).

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्लोकं वै दिवं ह्येष पुराणे निश्चयो गतः । भूतस्याधिपतिश्चाग्निस्ततो भूतपतिः स्मृतः
verses.transliteration: svarlokaṃ vai divaṃ hyeṣa purāṇe niścayo gataḥ / bhūtasyādhipatiścāgnistato bhūtapatiḥ smṛtaḥ
verses.translation: When a Kalpa ofVairajaka (i.e. pertaining to Brahma) passes by in the world of Brahma, the Vairaja (? Brahma) allots the SthSna in the Avyakta (Unmanifest one) Thus they (Devas etc.) in accordance with the posteriority and priority obtaining in the "Brahmaloka resort to the Vairajalokas after going and returning ten times.
verses.wordMeaning: When a Kalpa ofVairajaka (i.e. pertaining to Brahma) passes by in the world of Brahma,…
verses.commentary: Sense: When a Kalpa ofVairajaka (i.e. pertaining to Brahma) passes by in the world of Brahma,…

verses.sanskrit: वायुर्भुवश्चाधिपतिस्तेन वायुर्भुवस्पतिः । दिवस्य सूर्यो ऽधिपतिस्तेन सूर्यो दिवस्पतिः
verses.transliteration: vāyurbhuvaścādhipatistena vāyurbhuvaspatiḥ / divasya sūryo 'dhipatistena sūryo divaspatiḥ
verses.translation: They abide in the body of Brahma from which it is impossible to return. After reaching that world full of meditation, they attain the Supreme Bliss of Brahman. 1 Thereby they gain immortality.
verses.wordMeaning: They abide in the body of Brahma from which it is impossible to return. After reaching that world full of meditation, they attain the Supreme Bliss of Brahman. 1 Thereby they gain immortality.
verses.commentary: Sense: They abide in the body of Brahma from which it is impossible to return. After reaching that world full of meditation, they attain the Supreme Bliss of Brahman. 1 Thereby they gain immortality.

verses.sanskrit: महेति व्यात्दृतेनैव महर्लोकस्ततो ऽभवत् । विनिवृत्ताधिकारणां देवानां तत्र वै क्षयः
verses.transliteration: maheti vyātdṛtenaiva maharlokastato 'bhavat / vinivṛttādhikāraṇāṃ devānāṃ tatra vai kṣayaḥ
verses.translation: VV. 77-89 descibc the condition of the persons who reach Satya (= Brahma) Loka. This Purana supports the state of Liberation described in Brahma Sutras IV. 4.17-21 in that the Liberated soul has all the advantages and specialities of Brahma except his power to create the world etc (vide VV. 80-83).
verses.wordMeaning: VV. 77-89 descibc the condition of the persons who reach Satya (= Brahma) Loka. This Purana supports the state of Liberation described in Brahma Sutras IV.…
verses.commentary: Sense: VV. 77-89 descibc the condition of the persons who reach Satya (= Brahma) Loka. This Purana supports the state of Liberation described in Brahma Sutras IV.…

verses.sanskrit: जनस्तु पञ्चमो लोकस्तस्माज्जायन्ति वै जनाः । तासां स्वायंभुवाद्यानां प्रजानां जननाज्जनः
verses.transliteration: janastu pañcamo lokastasmājjāyanti vai janāḥ / tāsāṃ svāyaṃbhuvādyānāṃ prajānāṃ jananājjanaḥ
verses.translation: Thus the Devas and Sages partake of i.e. worship
verses.wordMeaning: Thus the Devas and Sages partake of i.e. worship
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus the Devas and Sages partake of i.e. worship

verses.sanskrit: ये ते स्वायंभुवाद्या हि पुरस्तात्परिकीर्त्तिताः । कल्प एते यदा लोके प्रतिष्ठन्ति तदा तपः
verses.transliteration: ye te svāyaṃbhuvādyā hi purastātparikīrttitāḥ / kalpa ete yadā loke pratiṣṭhanti tadā tapaḥ
verses.translation: They are Urdhvareras (those who have sublimated their sexual energy). They do not have anything which can slay them again (i.e. they are deathless). Their faith evolved J}y_rerjeated holy rites s indicated in the Vedantas (Upanisads
